name: com.obriym-crm/mcp
title: Obriym CRM
description: Operate Obriym CRM from your AI assistant: leads, deals, orders, catalog, stock, marketplaces.

tools.name: search_leads
tools.description: List and search this workspace's leads, filtered by text/status/source/created-date/stale and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, name, contact, company, status, source, assignee, tags, next-action, isStale, timestamps) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }, newest first. Use get_lead to fetch notes, position and score for one lead by id.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of results per page (1-100). Default 20.

from.description: Only leads created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z).

q.description: Free-text search over lead name, email, phone, or company. Omit for no text filter.

source.description: Filter by lead source key (e.g. website, referral, telegram). Use list_lead_sources to see the workspace's keys. Omit for all sources.

status.description: Filter by lead status. Omit to return every status. Allowed: new, contacted, qualified, unqualified, converted.

stale.description: Set true to return only stale leads: not unqualified/converted and either past their next-action date or untouched for more than 7 days.

to.description: Only leads created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z).

tools.name: get_lead
tools.description: Fetch one CRM lead in the selected workspace by lead id, including status, source, assignee, tags, custom fields, score, notes and next action. Use search_leads first when you only know a name, email, phone or company.

id.description: The lead id returned by search_leads.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List customer conversations across every connected channel (Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and comments, Telegram, OLX, Prom, eBay, Threads replies, the B2B portal, buyer order pages …). One row per lead and channel, newest first: { leadId, leadName, channel, lastMessageAt, lastMessageText (first 300 characters), lastDirection (inbound = from the customer), awaitingReply (the customer wrote last) } plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Open conversations only — converted or disqualified leads and closed threads are left out. Filter by channel, by awaitingReply, or by a text match on the customer's name or last message. Read-only: replies are written by a person in the CRM Inbox, this server cannot send messages. Use get_lead_conversation to read one thread's messages and get_lead for the lead card.

awaitingReply.description: True returns only conversations whose last message is from the customer and still wait for an answer.

channel.description: Channel slug to keep, as returned in the channel field of earlier results (e.g. instagram, telegram, olx). Omit for all channels.

query.description: Text to match against the customer's name or the last message.

tools.name: get_lead_conversation
tools.description: Read one lead's customer messages, oldest to newest: { at, channel, direction (inbound = from the customer, outbound = sent by the business), text (up to 2000 characters; truncated is true when cut), media ({ kind, contentType, name } or null — the file itself is never returned) }. A person who writes on two channels has two separate conversations: pass channel to read one, omit it to get all channels interleaved by time. Returns the most recent `limit` messages (default 30, max 100). Use it before drafting a reply or to answer what the customer asked. Read-only — this server cannot send messages. Use list_conversations to find leads with messages and get_lead for the lead card.

channel.description: Channel slug to read (e.g. instagram, telegram, olx), as returned by list_conversations. Omit for every channel.

leadId.description: The lead id returned by list_conversations or search_leads.

limit.description: How many of the newest messages to return (default 30).

tools.name: search_deals
tools.description: List and search pipeline deals, filtered by stage/owner/company/contact/stale and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, title, stage, amount, probability, owner, company, contact, next-action, isStale) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Use get_deal to fetch one deal's full detail by id.

companyId.description: Filter to deals linked to this company id (from search_companies).

contactId.description: Filter to deals linked to this contact id (from search_contacts).

ownerId.description: Filter to deals owned by this workspace member's user id.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of deals per page (1-100). Default 25.

q.description: Free-text search over the deal title. Omit for no text filter.

stageId.description: Filter to deals in this pipeline stage id (from list_pipeline_stages).

stale.description: Set "true" to return only stale deals (past their next-action date or long untouched).

tools.name: get_deal
tools.description: Fetch one pipeline deal in the selected workspace by deal id, including stage, value, probability and linked company/contact data when present. Use search_deals first when you only know the title or related customer.

id.description: The deal id returned by search_deals.

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: List this workspace's orders, filtered by status/customer/created-date and paginated. Returns summary rows (externalId, status, currency, totalAmount, itemCount, timestamps, shipByAt: nullable ISO ship-by deadline) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }, newest first. Use get_order to fetch one order's full detail (line items, payments, shipments, returns) by externalId.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of results per page (1-100). Default 20.

customerExternalId.description: Filter to one storefront customer by their externalId (the id from the source system). Omit to list all customers' orders.

from.description: Only orders created at or after this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z).

status.description: Filter by order status. Omit to return every status. Allowed: pending, confirmed, processing, ready_to_ship, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded.

to.description: Only orders created at or before this ISO 8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z).

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Fetch full order detail in the selected workspace by externalId, including line items, payments, shipments, returns and shipByAt (recorded ISO ship-by deadline, or null when unknown; not the actual dispatch time). Use list_orders first when you only know the customer or date.

externalId.description: The order externalId returned by list_orders.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: List and search catalog products (active unless status says otherwise: draft, archived or any), filtered by text (name or SKU), barcode (barcode or EAN/GTIN) or having none (withoutBarcode), category/brand/collection/model (productGroupId — the other colours and sizes of one model)/size/color/stock/tag/type, by price in a given currency (priceCurrency with minPrice/maxPrice, read through the product's price list) or having no price in it (withoutPriceIn), by being on or off a marketplace channel (channel, onChannel), or by supplier and the supplier's last stock report (supplierId, supplierStock), sorted by name, price, newest or popularity (units sold in the last 90 days), and paginated. Returns each product's catalog fields — price and prices per currency, stock (null when the shop does not count it; see trackInventory), availability, variant fields (productGroupId, color, size, material and the rest), attributes (every characteristic), category, brand — plus its model, warehouse and supplier by name, storageBin (the place in that warehouse where it lies — code and description, null when it has none) and supplierOffers (what the supplier last said: quantity, restock date, purchase price, state), and pagination { page, perPage, total }. A full row is heavy: pass fields to receive only the parts you read (id is always included). Use get_product to fetch one product's full detail by id or SKU.

brandId.description: Filter to one brand by its id. Empty string means any brand.

categoryId.description: Filter to one category by its id. Empty string means any category.

collection.description: Filter to the products of one collection, by its slug from GET /collections. Only a collection that is visible and in season matches — an unknown, hidden or out-of-season slug is reported as not found, exactly like GET /collections/{slug}. Empty means no collection filter.

color.description: Filter to products whose color equals this value, ignoring letter case (the product's own color field, not a free-form attribute). Empty means any color.

inStock.description: Set "true" to return only products with stock available. Empty means include out-of-stock.

maxPrice.description: Only products priced at or below this amount — in the workspace currency, or in priceCurrency when you pass it.

minPrice.description: Only products priced at or above this amount — in the workspace currency, or in priceCurrency when you pass it.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of products per page (1-100). Default 20.

q.description: Free-text search over product name and SKU. Empty for no text filter.

productGroupId.description: Filter to the variants of one model: products whose productGroupId equals this value exactly. It is the merchant's (or supplier's) own model code, so letter case is part of it. Use it to render the other colours and sizes of the product a buyer is looking at. Empty means any model.

size.description: Filter to products whose size equals this value, ignoring letter case (the product's own size field). Empty means any size.

sort.description: Sort order. Empty sorts by name. Allowed: name_asc, name_desc, price_asc, price_desc, newest, popular — popular ranks by units sold in confirmed, processing, ready-to-ship, shipped or delivered orders over the last 90 days. Ties break by name.

status.description: Filter by catalog status. Empty keeps the storefront default of active only. Use "draft" to find products waiting to be reviewed (marketplace imports and unknown SKUs from orders land there), or "any" for every status.

stockState.description: Filter by stock state, for products that track inventory. "low" returns products at or under their reorder threshold; "out" returns products with nothing left. Empty applies no stock-state filter.

tag.description: Filter to products carrying this tag. Empty means any tag.

type.description: Filter by product type. Empty for any; "simple" or "bundle".

warehouseId.description: Filter to products in one warehouse by its id, from the warehouse list. Use "none" for products assigned to no warehouse — they match no id, so nothing else surfaces them. Empty means any warehouse. An id absent from this workspace is reported as an error, never as an empty result.

supplierId.description: Only products bought from this supplier — an id from list_suppliers — or "none" for products with no supplier. Omit for any supplier.

supplierStock.description: Only products whose supplier feed (e.g. Sipec) last reported this: in_stock (quantity above zero), arriving (none now, a restock date given), out_of_stock (none, no date), unknown (the supplier has not said). Omit for any.

barcode.description: Only products whose barcode or EAN/GTIN equals this value (exact; leading zeros are ignored, so a 12-digit UPC finds its 13-digit EAN form). Omit for any.

withoutBarcode.description: true = only products with neither a barcode nor an EAN/GTIN — the ones a marketplace refuses without an exemption. Omit for any.

withoutPriceIn.description: ISO 4217 code such as EUR. Only products with NO price in this currency (no price-list row and it is not their own currency) — the ones a store in that currency cannot sell. Omit for any.

priceCurrency.description: ISO 4217 code such as EUR. Makes minPrice/maxPrice compare the price the product has in THIS currency (its price list, else its own price when that is its currency) and keeps only products that are sold in it. Without minPrice/maxPrice it simply keeps the products sold in that currency. Omit to compare the workspace-currency price.

channel.description: A marketplace slug from list_marketplaces. Keeps the ACTIVE products that are on that channel (the same definition list_channel_products uses), or with onChannel=false those that are not. Omit for any.

onChannel.description: Used with channel: true (default) = only products on the channel, false = only products NOT on it. Ignored without channel.

fields.description: Which parts of each product to return; omit for the full row. `id` is always included. A hundred full rows weigh hundreds of kilobytes (description, translations, attributes, images, supplier offers), so when you only match or list products ask for what you read, for example ["name","sku","status","price","currency","stock","availability"]. `prices` is the price per currency, `stock` is null when the shop does not count it (see `trackInventory`), `supplierOffers` is what the supplier last said.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Fetch one catalog product in the selected workspace by product id or SKU — returned in any status (draft, active, or archived; check the status field) — with every catalog field: prices, cost, stock and trackInventory, availability, variant fields, all attributes (characteristics) and translations, identifiers, weight and dimensions, images, videos, bundle components and related products; plus its model, warehouse and supplier by name, storageBin (the place in that warehouse where it lies — code and description, null when it has none; a label, not a quantity), supplierOffers (what the supplier last said: quantity, restock date, purchase price, state), locations (the units in each warehouse — quantity, reserved by open orders, available, status — adding up to stock; null when the workspace keeps one count per product), fulfillment (what Amazon FBA holds — ready to ship, inbound, reserved, unfulfillable, when last read — never part of stock; null when off), every sales channel with its listing and moderation state, the collections it is in and its model's review summary; channelTexts (the title and bullet points written for a channel such as Amazon, per language), safetyDocuments (safety PDFs a marketplace receives) and gpsr (the manufacturer and EU responsible person with their emails, each from the brand, else the supplier). A bundle's stock and cost are derived from its components. Provide exactly one known identifier; use search_products first when unsure (search covers active products only).

id.description: The product id returned by search_products.

sku.description: The product SKU returned by search_products.

tools.name: get_dashboard_overview
tools.description: Return the operational 'what needs attention today' snapshot for this workspace: active/qualified/stale lead counts, pipeline value, weighted forecast and overdue activities. Takes no arguments. Use get_report for period trend analytics instead.

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: Return one aggregated analytics report over a period for this workspace, selected by the report parameter: lead_source_conversion, pipeline_velocity, team_performance, revenue_trend, product_sales (units, revenue and gross margin per brand/category/SKU) or stock_valuation (units on hand and their value per warehouse, per cost currency). Each returns aggregated rows (no per-record data); days tunes the look-back for lead_source_conversion, team_performance and product_sales, months the span for revenue_trend; pipeline_velocity and stock_valuation take no period. Use get_dashboard_overview for today's operational snapshot instead.

months.description: Number of months for the revenue-trend report (default 6).

report.description: Which analytics report to return. lead_source_conversion: leads and conversion rate per source (uses days). pipeline_velocity: average time deals spend in each stage. team_performance: revenue and activity per member (uses days). revenue_trend: won revenue by month (uses months). product_sales: units, revenue and gross margin per brand, category and SKU, plus a trend (uses days). stock_valuation: units on hand and their value at weighted-average cost, per warehouse and per cost currency — currencies are reported separately and never added together (takes no period).

tools.name: search_contacts
tools.description: List and search this workspace's contacts, filtered by company/owner/tag, sorted and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, firstName, lastName, email, phone, jobTitle, company, owner, tags) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Use get_contact to fetch one contact's full detail by id.

companyId.description: Filter to contacts at this company id (from search_companies).

ownerId.description: Filter to contacts owned by this workspace member's user id.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of contacts per page (1-100). Default 25.

q.description: Free-text search over name, email and company. Omit for no text filter.

sortBy.description: Field to sort by. Default name. Allowed: name, email, createdAt.

tag.description: Filter to contacts carrying this tag. Omit for any tag.

tools.name: get_contact
tools.description: Fetch one CRM contact in the selected workspace by contact id, including company, owner, tags and communication fields when present. Use search_contacts first when you only know a name, email or phone.

id.description: The contact id returned by search_contacts.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: List and search this workspace's companies, filtered by industry/status/owner, sorted and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, name, industry, size, status, owner, contactCount) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Use get_company to fetch one company's full detail by id.

industry.description: Filter to companies in this industry. Omit for any industry.

ownerId.description: Filter to companies owned by this workspace member's user id.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of companies per page (1-100). Default 25.

q.description: Free-text search over the company name. Omit for no text filter.

sortDir.description: Sort direction by name. Default asc.

status.description: Filter by relationship status. Omit for any. Allowed: prospect, active, inactive.

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: Fetch one CRM company in the selected workspace by company id, including status, industry, owner and contact links when present. Use search_companies first when you only know the company name.

id.description: The company id returned by search_companies.

tools.name: list_activities
tools.description: List this workspace's activities (tasks, calls, meetings, emails, notes), filtered by type/assignee/overdue/completion/linked-entity and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, type, title, priority, dueDate, completed, assignee, linked lead/contact/company/deal, isOverdue) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Use get_activity to fetch one activity's full detail by id.

assignedTo.description: Filter to activities assigned to this workspace member's user id.

companyId.description: Filter to activities linked to this company id (from search_companies).

completed.description: Filter by completion: "true" only completed, "false" only open. Omit for both.

contactId.description: Filter to activities linked to this contact id (from search_contacts).

dealId.description: Filter to activities linked to this deal id (from search_deals).

leadId.description: Filter to activities linked to this lead id (from search_leads).

overdue.description: Set "true" to return only overdue activities (past due date, not completed).

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of activities per page (1-100). Default 20.

q.description: Free-text search over the activity title. Omit for no text filter.

type.description: Filter by activity type. Omit for any. Allowed: task, call, meeting, email, note.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: Fetch one CRM activity in the selected workspace by activity id, including type, due date, completion state, assignee and linked entity. Use list_activities first when you only know the related lead/deal/contact.

id.description: The activity id returned by list_activities.

tools.name: list_customers
tools.description: List CRM customers: companies that bought — a purchase order (processing, ready to ship, shipped, delivered or refunded, or with a settled payment) or a won deal that never became an order. Filter by health, lifetime-value bucket, owner, name search or minimum won deals; sorted by lifetime value and paginated. Returns summary rows (id, name, health, lifetimeValue = completed-order revenue plus won deals without an order, purchases = purchase orders plus won deals without an order, repeat = two or more purchases, lastPurchaseAt, wonDealsCount = every won deal, lastActivityAt, owner) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Read-only. Use get_customer to fetch one customer's detail by company id; use list_people_customers for people who bought without a company (shop buyers).

health.description: Filter by customer health. Omit for any. Allowed: healthy, at_risk, churned.

ltv.description: Filter by lifetime-value bucket. Omit for any. Allowed: lt10k, 10k50k, gt50k.

ownerId.description: Filter to customers owned by this workspace member's user id.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of customers per page (1-100). Default 25.

q.description: Free-text search over the customer company name. Omit for no text filter.

sortDir.description: Sort direction by lifetime value. Default desc (highest first).

wonDealsMin.description: Only customers with at least this many won deals (orders are not counted here).

tools.name: get_customer
tools.description: Fetch one CRM customer summary in the selected workspace by company id: a company that bought (a purchase order — processing, ready to ship, shipped, delivered or refunded, or with a settled payment — or a won deal that never became an order). Returns health, lifetimeValue (completed-order revenue plus won deals without an order), purchases (purchase orders plus won deals without an order), repeat (two or more purchases), lastPurchaseAt and wonDealsCount (every won deal). Read-only; a company with no purchase is not found. Use list_customers first when you only know the company name; use get_person_customer for a person who bought without a company.

companyId.description: The company/customer id returned by list_customers.

tools.name: list_people_customers
tools.description: List people (CRM contacts) who bought without a company — shop buyers: a purchase order without a company (processing, ready to ship, shipped, delivered or refunded, or with a settled payment) or a won deal of theirs without a company that never became an order. A company's purchases never count for the person who represents it. Filter by health, lifetime-value bucket, repeat (two or more purchases) or search over name, email and phone; sorted by lifetime value and paginated. Returns rows (id = contact id, firstName, lastName, email, phone, health, lifetimeValue, purchases, repeat, firstPurchaseAt, lastPurchaseAt, lastActivityAt) plus pagination { page, perPage, total }. Read-only. Use get_person_customer for one person by contact id; use list_customers for companies.

health.description: Filter by customer health. Omit for any. Allowed: healthy, at_risk, churned.

ltv.description: Filter by lifetime-value bucket. Omit for any. Allowed: lt10k, 10k50k, gt50k.

page.description: 1-based page number of results to return. Default 1.

perPage.description: Number of people per page (1-100). Default 25.

q.description: Free-text search over the person's first name, last name, email and phone. Omit for no text filter.

repeat.description: true = only people with two or more purchases; false or omitted = everyone.

sortDir.description: Sort direction by lifetime value. Default desc (highest first).

tools.name: get_person_customer
tools.description: Fetch one person who bought without a company, by contact id: health, lifetimeValue (completed-order revenue plus won deals without an order), purchases, repeat, firstPurchaseAt, lastPurchaseAt and contact details. Read-only; a contact who never bought without a company is not found. Use list_people_customers or search_contacts first when you only know the name, email or phone; use get_customer for a company.

contactId.description: The contact/customer id returned by list_people_customers.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List this workspace catalog categories as a flat array, each with id, name, slug, parentId (null for a root category), description, googleProductCategory, imageUrl, translations and marketplaceCategories (the Prom, Rozetka, OLX, Amazon and Google Merchant category ids already linked, each as { id, label } or null). Categories are workspace-global, not per warehouse. Use a category id here as the categoryId for create_product/update_product, or as the search_products category filter. Use get_category for one category's product and subcategory counts, and search_marketplace_categories to find a marketplace category id to link.

tools.name: get_category
tools.description: Fetch one catalog category by id: name, slug, parent, description, image, translations, the linked marketplace category ids (marketplaceCategories: Prom, Rozetka, OLX, Amazon, Google Merchant, each { id, label } or null), its direct subcategories (children), and productCount and subcategoryCount. Read-only. Use list_categories first to find the id, and call this before delete_category to see what a deletion would affect.

id.description: The category id returned by list_categories.

tools.name: search_marketplace_categories
tools.description: Find the category id a marketplace uses, to link it to a catalog category. Read-only. Pass the platform (prom, rozetka, olx, amazon, google_merchant or etsy) and a query, or for OLX, Rozetka and Etsy a parentId to browse one level of the tree (no query and no parentId lists the top level). Sources differ: Google Merchant searches the bundled Google product taxonomy and needs no connection; Etsy searches Etsy's seller taxonomy, shared by every shop; OLX, Rozetka and Amazon ask the marketplace through the connected adapter (connected tells you whether one exists); Prom publishes no category directory, so only rubrics already seen on this merchant's own Prom listings are returned (partial tells you the list may be incomplete, note explains why). OLX and Etsy only accept a LEAF category: check isLeaf and keep browsing with parentId until you reach one. Results are candidates for the USER to choose from: when several fit, show them and ask, never pick one silently. Then pass the chosen id in marketplaceCategories of update_category or create_category.

parentId.description: Browse one level of the marketplace tree under this id (OLX and Rozetka). Omit, together with query, to list the top level.

platform.description: The marketplace whose categories to look up.

query.description: Words describing the shelf, e.g. the CRM category's name ('кросівки', 'running shoes'). At least two characters.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: List this workspace catalog brands with id, name, description and website. Use a brand id here as the brandId for create_product/update_product, or as the search_products brand filter.

tools.name: list_warehouses
tools.description: List this workspace warehouses with id, name, description, phone, address (the street line), country (ISO code), city, postalCode, workingHours (free text), pickupEnabled (a self-pickup point), kind (own — the shop's stock; supplier — a supplier's showcase it sells from; fulfillment — a marketplace's warehouse such as Amazon FBA, kept by the marketplace and never a product's own), lowStockThreshold (null = each product's own mark) and allowNegative; stockPerWarehouse says whether the workspace keeps a count per warehouse. A product is filed under one primary warehouse, which decides the inventory-tracking default and which channels new products join. Use an id here as the warehouseId for create_product (never a fulfillment one), list_warehouse_stock or set_channel_warehouses.

tools.name: list_warehouse_stock
tools.description: List what lies in one warehouse of a workspace that keeps stock per warehouse, product by product: quantity, reservedQuantity (held by open orders), status (in_stock, low, out), threshold and the product's total stock, 50 per page with counts of products, units, low and out over the whole warehouse. For an Amazon FBA warehouse the figures are Amazon's from its last hourly read (quantity = ready to ship + reserved). Read-only. Use list_warehouses for the id, get_product for one product across every warehouse; refused when the workspace keeps one count per product.

filter.description: Which rows: all (default), low — at or below the warehouse's low-stock mark, or out — none available here after reservations.

q.description: Search by product name or SKU (optional).

warehouseId.description: The warehouse id returned by list_warehouses.

tools.name: get_stock_sources
tools.description: Read which warehouses the workspace sells from: orders.warehouseIds — the list an order with no channel list takes its units from, in order (null = each product's primary warehouse); channels — each marketplace's own list, which is both what it publishes (units there minus reservations) and where its orders take units (a channel absent here publishes each product's total); platforms — the channels that accept a list; warehouses — the own warehouses and supplier showcases a list may name. Lists apply only while stockPerWarehouse is true. Read-only. Use preview_channel_warehouses then set_channel_warehouses to change a channel, set_order_warehouses for orders.

tools.name: list_marketplaces
tools.description: List every marketplace connected to this workspace with its setup state, health, last activity, any current sync error with `problem` (its kind, whether a person must reconnect the account, and what to do), `partialFailure` ({ failed, sent, sample, whatToDo }) when the last run reached the marketplace but part of it was refused (health stays active for that, so check it), orders revenue per currency, leads, product counts on the channel and how many imported products are waiting to be reviewed. advertising: true marks a channel where nothing is sold (Google Merchant), so its zero revenue is structural. Answers 'which channels do I sell on and is anything broken'. Takes no arguments. Use get_marketplace for one channel in detail, list_channel_products for what is on it, and check_channel_readiness for what it will refuse.

tools.name: get_marketplace
tools.description: Fetch one connected marketplace in detail: every adapter on it with its setup state, last poll, last poll error, last catalog-sync outcome (`sync`, whose `lastSuccessAt` is the last run without a connection error — it survives failures, so it says how long a channel has been broken; `notAttempted` counts matched listings the run had no time left for and `truncated` true means not every listing was read — the next run continues, so a short `updated` with a large `notAttempted` is an unfinished run, not a skipped change) and last product import, a classified `problem` (kind, needsReconnect, platformMessage, whatToDo) when anything failed, `partialFailure` ({ failed, sent, sample, whatToDo }) when the last run connected fine but the marketplace refused some products (health stays active), and for google_merchant `sync.failedSample` (up to 5 refused products with Google's own message; the reason for those only, not every refused one), plus the channel sales, leads and product counts. For google_merchant each adapter also has `moderation` — what Google decided about the products the CRM sent, as the hourly check stored it (approved, pending, limited, rejected, missing, otherTarget, offChannel, topIssues, lastCheckedAt, complete, lastError; null before the first check; complete false means only part of the catalog was read) — and `setup`: setupBlock (what stands in the way: not_connected, no_account, no_country, no_terms, not_armed — owner setup, not an outage), armed, lastPreviewAt, feedLabel, currency, termsAccepted, productUrlTemplate and contentLanguageOverride. Reads stored state only, never calls the marketplace. Use list_marketplaces first to see which platforms are connected, list_channel_products for the products on the channel and check_channel_readiness for what would be refused.

tools.name: adjust_stock
tools.description: Move a product stock by a relative delta (negative to write off, positive to add) with a reason, and record it in the stock history. This is the correct tool for a correction, a write-off or damage — it never sets an absolute number, so an order committing at the same moment is not overwritten. The reason decides the direction: write_off, damage and return_to_supplier must carry a negative delta, opening_balance a positive one, while correction and other accept either; a delta that contradicts its reason is rejected. Any other word is your own vocabulary and is accepted in either direction. The product must already track inventory; a product that does not returns a conflict rather than having tracking switched on for it. A bundle also returns a conflict: its stock is derived from its components, so adjust each component instead. Pass a stable externalId to make a retry idempotent. The new stock is pushed to every connected sales channel. The result echoes the operating workspace.

Reads eBay, never writes. Use search_products first for the ids; after a fix with update_product, upsert_product_prices, upsert_product_attributes or upsert_product_translation, call it again — a reason can change or clear.

tools.name: inspect_amazon_listings
tools.description: Report how the workspace's Amazon offers stand for a buyer and what Amazon says is wrong with them. Per product linked to an Amazon listing: stage (active; search_suppressed = buyable but hidden from search, usually no main image; inactive = Seller Central's 'Non attivo'; no_offer = the listing exists but Amazon shows no offer on it yet (Seller Central's 'Offerta mancante'), usual for a few hours after it is created, so re-check before changing anything; suppressed = taken down by Amazon; missing = no offer under that SKU any more; null = never checked), action (fix_issues when Amazon reports an ERROR), issues (code, severity, message, the attributes involved, Amazon's enforcement such as SEARCH_SUPPRESSED), amazonSku (the seller SKU Amazon knows the offer by when it differs from the CRM SKU, e.g. a variation child linked by its barcode), the ASIN and when it was checked, and markets (per Amazon store: stage, action, the price and quantity it shows); plus a count per stage over the whole channel. Worst first, 100 rows a page: total, limit, offset and hasMore say whether to read on with offset; stage filters (with marketplaceId, the stage and action are that store's). For a listing Amazon started by itself, stage no_offer on a store is a shell with no offer: publish_amazon_listings with that marketplaceId adds the offer to it (price, quantity and condition come from the product). With refresh=true it asks Amazon first (a read; writes only the CRM's record of the answer). It never changes an offer: send photos and GPSR contacts with preview_amazon_listing_content then update_amazon_listing_content; the rest is fixed in Seller Central or on the product. Use list_channel_products for price and stock on the channel and check_channel_readiness for products not yet listed.

refresh.description: true asks Amazon now (summaries, issues, relationships) and records the answer before reporting; false reports what the CRM recorded on its last check, which runs hourly. Use true after the merchant fixed something in Seller Central.

Rows report status (ready, nothing, blocked, rejected, failed), attributes, issues, skipped, filled, stillMissing and untranslated. Measurement rows additionally show measurements (field key/title, before and after values with units) and measurementPreview. To send measurements, copy each ready product id and its measurementPreview into measurementPreviews on update_amazon_listing_content; a changed CRM or Amazon value requires a fresh preview. Missing measurements are not invented, ambiguous values are not replaced, and another store is preserved. Set missing Amazon answers with get_amazon_fields and set_amazon_field_values; edit catalog measurements on the product. Use inspect_amazon_listings to find existing offers, then update_amazon_listing_content to send ready rows. Needs a selected Amazon marketplace, but no write arming.

A price for one channel only is set_product_channel_price; see all of a product's prices with get_product_pricing. Saves through the same product-card operation as the CRM form, with a version check (on CONFLICT re-read the product and retry), and the new price reaches connected channels like a manual edit. Never invent a value: ask the user. Saves through the same product-card operation as the CRM form, with a version check (on CONFLICT re-read and retry). On a product that belongs to a model: when it is the model's only article, the characteristics are the model's and change for the model; when the model has other articles, a value set here applies to this article only — a characteristic shared by every article is changed on the model card. For a product that belongs to a model the translation is the model's, so every article of it changes. tools.name: archive_products
tools.description: Archive up to 100 products — this is how an AI client removes a product. It leaves sale and every sales channel's feed, and nothing is erased: update_product with status active or draft restores it. Hard deletion is not available over MCP. A product that a non-archived bundle is made of is NOT archived: it is listed in heldByBundle with the bundles that contain it — archive or change those bundles first. Archiving also asks Prom to take the product's listings down; notAttempted counts takedowns not reached in time. To end a live eBay listing use withdraw_ebay_listings. Returns { affected, skipped, notAttempted, heldByBundle } — skipped products were already archived. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

tools.name: update_amazon_listing_content
tools.description: Send selected listing data to up to 25 EXISTING Amazon offers. Real external writes under the owner-armed content direction and AI publishing gate; no new listing is created. The default six parts keep their behavior: photos, GPSR, Amazon texts, safety documents, shipping, and fill-only attributes. Explicit parts ["measurements"] refreshes changed item/package weight and dimensions only: preview_amazon_listing_content first, then pass ready product ids and their measurementPreview values in measurementPreviews. Stale or missing measurement previews are refused before any outbound write; the exact payload is validated by Amazon again before sending. Other stores and unknown measurement metadata are preserved; missing or ambiguous measurements are not cleared. Returns per-product rows and notAttempted ids for a later bounded call. sent means accepted for processing, not verified buyer-visible data; inspect_amazon_listings after processing. Repeating an unchanged measurement is a no-op. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store; a send needs it when several stores are open for listing-data updates.

parts.description: What to send: images (main photo and up to 8 more), gpsr (manufacturer and EU responsible person), texts (Amazon title and bullet points), documents (safety PDFs), shipping (assigned shipping template and handling time), attributes (fill missing listing facts only), measurements (explicitly refresh changed item/package weight and dimensions from CRM facts and Amazon field answers). Default: the original six parts; measurements must be named explicitly. Missing, invalid or ambiguous measurements are never cleared or guessed. For measurement sends, pass measurementPreviews from the read-only preview. Package measurements are separate from the item and from the outer parcel used to buy a shipping label.

tools.name: set_channel_membership
tools.description: Mark or unmark up to 100 products for one connected sales channel (prom, rozetka, ebay, olx, …). It changes what the CRM intends to send: on Prom and Rozetka the next feed pull adds or drops the product; on eBay it only makes the product a channel member — a listing exists only after create_ebay_drafts and publish_ebay_drafts. It never arms a sync. Adding picks up active products only. Returns { affected, skipped } — skipped were already in that state. Refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

listed.description: true marks the products for this channel; false unmarks them. This only changes what the CRM intends to send — it never arms a sync and never creates a listing by itself. Unmarking a product on Prom drops it from the next feed pull.

platform.description: The connected sales channel to change membership on (e.g. prom, rozetka, ebay, olx).

productIds.description: The exact products to change, at most 100 ids fetched with search_products.

tools.name: push_google_merchant_catalog
tools.description: Send this workspace's catalog, or just the products you name, to Google Merchant Center now — the same as the "Update now" button on the Google Merchant channel page. It is a REAL write to Google: products become or stay visible in Google Shopping. It runs only the product push the owner has ALREADY armed on the connection (otherwise it is refused) and only after the owner accepted Google's terms; it never arms anything and never changes settings. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing. It is rarely needed: an hourly job sends the catalog anyway, so use it only when a fix must reach Google before the next run. To get one fixed product to Google immediately pass productIds (1 to 25): only those products are sent, and the result is { adapterId, adapterName, sent, failed, blocked, notOnChannel } — sent and failed (with Google's own message) name each product, blocked carries the readiness reason, notOnChannel lists ids that are not active channel members; this does not change the channel's last-run summary. Without productIds the whole catalog is sent, never-sent and changed products first, bounded by a time budget — if truncated is true, call it again. Returns { adapterId, adapterName, outcome } where outcome has pushed, failed, blocked, ready, total, truncated, lastSyncAt and failedSample (up to 5 refused products with Google's message). A failure that came back from Google carries reason (for example auth_expired) with details.needsReconnect and details.whatToDo: auth_expired, such as invalid_grant, means a person must reconnect the Google account on the adapter page, and retrying will not help. Use check_channel_readiness first to see which products would be withheld, and get_marketplace for the last run. Not idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

adapterId.description: The Google Merchant connection to push (adapter id, listed by get_marketplace for google_merchant). Omit it when the workspace has exactly one Google Merchant connection — the server picks it; with several connections the call is refused until one is named.

productIds.description: Product ids (1 to 25) to send to Google right now instead of the whole catalog. Use it to get a fixed product to Google at once. Each id must be an active member of the Google channel; others come back as notOnChannel, products the readiness rule withholds as blocked (with the reason), and Google's refusals as failed (with Google's own message). Omit it to push the whole catalog in priority order.

tools.name: create_ebay_drafts
tools.description: Create eBay DRAFT offers for up to 25 products — real writes to the seller's eBay account, but nothing is buyer-visible until publish_ebay_drafts. Run inspect_ebay_listings first and pass only products whose nextAction is create_draft and ready is true. Each product is attempted on its own: returns created, failed (each with a reason to look up in remediation.ebayPlaybook) and notAttempted (not reached in the time budget — call again with those ids). Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing, and while draft creation is not armed on the eBay connection. Not idempotent: a product that already has a draft fails with alreadyListed. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: Omit this when the eBay connection sells on exactly one marketplace — the server fills it in automatically. Pass one of the audit's armed ebayDraftSetup.marketplaceIds only when several marketplaces are armed. This is a MARKETPLACE id (e.g. EBAY_DE, EBAY_IT) — never the eBay CONNECTION/adapter id.

productIds.description: The exact products to create eBay draft offers for, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. This creates drafts only and never makes them live.

tools.name: publish_ebay_drafts
tools.description: Make the eBay DRAFT offers of up to 25 products LIVE and buyer-visible — a real publication on the seller's account. The item and offer are refreshed from the current product first, so a price, title, photo or characteristic fixed after the draft was made is published too. Pass only products whose nextAction from inspect_ebay_listings is publish_draft. Returns done, failed (with reasons) and notAttempted. Never tell the user a listing is live unless it is counted in done. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing. The result echoes the workspace.

productIds.description: Make each product's eBay DRAFT offer LIVE and buyer-visible, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. The item and offer are refreshed from current product data first, then published — this is a real, consequential publication, not a preview. Report every named per-product failure.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: recreate_ebay_drafts
tools.description: Delete each product's eBay draft and create a fresh one from its current data, for up to 25 products. Needed only when a draft must move to another category or eBay site, or the reason is ebayDraftOfferMissing or ebayNoOfferId — ordinary edits are picked up by publish_ebay_drafts. A live listing is refused. If the delete succeeds but the new draft fails, that product is left with no draft and its failure says so. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: Omit this when the eBay connection sells on exactly one marketplace — the server fills it in automatically. Pass one of the audit's armed ebayDraftSetup.marketplaceIds only when several are armed. This is a MARKETPLACE id (e.g. EBAY_DE) — never the eBay CONNECTION/adapter id.

productIds.description: Delete each product's existing eBay draft offer and create a fresh one from its CURRENT data, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. Use this when a draft must move to a different category or marketplace, or eBay rejected its offer and a plain retry will not fix it. A LIVE listing is refused. If the delete succeeds but the new create fails, the failure says so explicitly — that product is then on the channel with NO draft.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: delete_ebay_drafts
tools.description: Delete the eBay DRAFT offer of up to 25 products; a live listing is refused — end it with withdraw_ebay_listings first. The CRM product itself is untouched. Works even while draft creation is disarmed on the connection, but still needs the owner's AI publishing switch. Returns done, failed and notAttempted. The result echoes the workspace.

productIds.description: Delete the eBay DRAFT offer for each of these products, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. Only a product whose offer is still a draft is affected — a LIVE listing is refused; end it with withdraw_ebay_listings first if it must go.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: withdraw_ebay_listings
tools.description: End the LIVE eBay listing of up to 25 products: they stop being buyer-visible and their offers return to drafts — nothing is deleted, and publish_ebay_drafts can put them back. Needs the owner's AI publishing switch. Returns done, failed and notAttempted. The result echoes the workspace.

productIds.description: End each product's LIVE eBay listing, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. The listing stops being buyer-visible and its offer returns to a draft — it is NOT deleted.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: update_ebay_listings
tools.description: Re-send the LIVE eBay listing of up to 25 products from each product as it is now — title, description, photos, item specifics, condition, price, quantity and business policies — without ending the sale. Use after a listed product was corrected (update_product, upsert_product_translation, upsert_product_attributes, upsert_product_prices, set_channel_texts) and eBay should show it; a draft goes through publish_ebay_drafts instead, and the listing's eBay category never changes here (recreate_ebay_drafts does that). Every go-live gate runs again, so a missing required specific is named rather than left for eBay; a product whose eBay sync is paused is refused. Needs the owner's AI publishing switch and an armed listingCreate direction. eBay allows 250 revisions per listing a day. Returns done, failed (named, with reasons) and notAttempted. The result echoes the workspace.

productIds.description: Re-send each product's LIVE eBay listing from the product as it is now, at most 25 ids fetched with search_products. The sale continues; a draft (publish_ebay_drafts) or a product with no listing is refused by name.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: check_amazon_readiness
tools.description: Ask Amazon whether up to 25 products could be listed now — the same check as the Amazon channel page: the offline requirements (product type on the category, brand, a photo, the condition, a title of at most 75 characters), the price in the marketplace's currency, then Amazon's own dry run (VALIDATION_PREVIEW), which creates nothing. A product whose barcode Amazon already knows is checked as an OFFER on that existing item (ready rows carry its asin): only the condition and the price matter then, and a brand or category Amazon gates is refused with reason amazonListingRestricted and the approval links. Returns ready, blocked (reason, details, Amazon's sentence) and notAttemptedIds (call again with those). A blocked product's details also name what the Amazon product type still needs, found against Amazon's own schema before its dry run: missingFieldKeys (attribute keys), missingFields (their titles in the marketplace's language) and invalidFields. The CRM fills model_name (the model's code), list_price (the old price when higher, else the price, VAT included) and the item's dimensions itself; set anything else for Amazon with set_amazon_field_values (keys, kinds and allowed values from get_amazon_fields) — on the category or the model when every product shares the value. A characteristic named exactly like the field's title (upsert_product_attributes) also reaches Amazon, but characteristics are shown on the shop's site and every other channel, so keep them for real product facts. Needs a listing marketplace chosen on the Amazon connection; no arming. Then publish with publish_amazon_listings.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store. Language, currency and required fields are that store's own.

productIds.description: The products to check, at most 25 ids.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: search_amazon_catalog
tools.description: Find whether a product already exists in Amazon's catalog on the workspace's listing marketplace — by barcode (EAN/UPC/GTIN), by ASIN, or by keywords. Returns up to 10 matches with asin, title, brand, the product type and the first photo. A barcode match means publish_amazon_listings makes an OFFER on that item rather than a new product. Reads Amazon, never writes. Use search_products for the CRM's own catalog.

by.description: How to read query: barcode (8–14 digits), asin (e.g. B0ABCDEF12) or keywords (free text).

query.description: The barcode, ASIN or words to search for.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store. Language, currency and required fields are that store's own.

tools.name: publish_amazon_listings
tools.description: Create Amazon listings for up to 25 products — a REAL publication on the seller's Amazon account. Each product runs the full check again (Amazon's dry run included) and is refused with Amazon's own sentences if anything changed; a product whose barcode Amazon already knows becomes an offer on that existing item. Run check_amazon_readiness first and pass only ready products. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing, and while listing creation is not armed on the Amazon connection. Returns created (with the ASIN or SKU and, in submitted, the price, currency, quantity and fulfilment the listing was sent with — quantityOmitted says why no quantity went out: stockNotTracked or stockUnknown; an FBA offer's quantity is Amazon's own), failed (reason, details) and notAttemptedIds. created means Amazon ACCEPTED the submission for processing, not that the listing is live or buyable: Amazon finishes it asynchronously, so check the outcome later with inspect_amazon_listings and never tell the user a listing is live from this result alone. Not idempotent: a product already listed fails with alreadyListed. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Required when more than one store is open for this write; the store must have passed its own dry run on the Amazon connection.

productIds.description: The products to publish, at most 25 ready ids from check_amazon_readiness.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: sync_amazon_offers
tools.description: Push the CRM's current price and stock to the workspace's existing Amazon offers now; an hourly job does it anyway, so use it only when a change must reach Amazon before the next run. A price change — the product's own, its price list, or set_product_channel_price — reaches Amazon ONLY through this push (an instant update after an edit sends stock alone). Pass productIds after changing a set of products: their offers are looked up by SKU, which is far faster than the whole run; without productIds it is the same as the Amazon connection page's sync button and walks every offer on every store, which a single call often cannot finish. It runs only the directions the owner ALREADY armed (price push, stock push) and never arms anything: price only in the store's currency (with the product's Amazon channel price when one is set), stock only for products that track it and only for MFN offers (FBA stock is Amazon's). Offers Amazon shows on sale go first. A product taken off the channel or paused is skipped. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing. Returns matched (product × store pairs found), updated (sent and accepted), unchanged (Amazon already showed these numbers), failed, priceBlocked (no price in the store's currency), truncated (the offers were not all read) and notAttempted (the call ran out of time before these: call again — sending the same numbers again changes nothing on Amazon). Amazon applies an accepted change asynchronously, so the offer can show the old price for a while; check with inspect_amazon_listings refresh=true. The result echoes the workspace.

productIds.description: Only these products, at most 100 ids from search_products. Omit for every offer on the channel.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: withdraw_amazon_listings
tools.description: Take up to 25 products off sale on Amazon: the offer's quantity becomes 0 on every marketplace it exists on (nobody can buy it) — the offer is NOT deleted and keeps its history and reviews in Seller Central — and the product leaves the CRM's Amazon channel so the hourly push does not restore the quantity; adding it to the channel again (set_channel_membership) brings it back. Not gated on the owner's arming (taking an offer down never is), but refused until the owner switches on AI publishing. Returns per product: withdrawn, blocked (noListing, listingNotFound, variationParent, fulfilledByAmazon, noOffer = Amazon holds the item with no offer on it, so there is nothing to take off sale), rejected (Amazon's sentences) or failed; notAttempted to call again. With marketplaceIds only those stores are zeroed and the other stores keep selling; the product leaves the CRM's Amazon channel only when no store is left selling. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceIds.description: Only these Amazon stores, by id. The product keeps selling everywhere else and stays on the channel; publishing it on such a store again puts it back on sale. Omit to take it off every store.

productIds.description: The products to take off sale, at most 25 ids.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: set_amazon_listing_texts
tools.description: Set ONE product's title and selling points for Amazon, in the language of the workspace's Amazon marketplace (amazon.it → Italian). The title keeps to 75 characters (the workspace's rule — a product whose own name is longer cannot be listed without it); up to 5 points of at most 500 characters. Write only what the user stated or approved, in the marketplace's language. title null with bulletPoints [] removes them; bulletPoints left out keeps the saved points, and Amazon then gets the product name and characteristics. Saved in the CRM only: a new listing carries them; an existing offer gets them through update_amazon_listing_content with parts ["texts"]. For a whole model (every colour at once, and the title of its Amazon parent) or for eBay, use set_channel_texts. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

bulletPoints.description: Up to 5 selling points, in order; empty strings are dropped. Omit to keep the points already saved (changing only the title); [] removes them.

productId.description: A product id returned by search_products.

title.description: The Amazon title, at most 75 characters; null to use the product name.

tools.name: set_product_safety_documents
tools.description: Replace ONE product's safety documents (EU GPSR) — the whole list: a document left out is removed. Each is a public https link to a PDF that marketplaces fetch themselves (Amazon's compliance_media), its kind (safety_information, user_manual, declaration_of_conformity, certificate) and the language it is written in. At most 10. Use only links the user gave — never invent a document. A new Amazon listing carries them; an existing offer gets them through update_amazon_listing_content with parts ["documents"]. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

locale.description: The language it is written in (ISO 639-1).

name.description: A short name shown in the CRM.

url.description: A public https link to the PDF.

documents.description: The product's full list of safety documents.

productId.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: check_amazon_variation_family
tools.description: The model's active articles become ONE listing with variations on one Amazon store — Amazon's "variation family"; call it a model with variations when talking to the user: a parent whose SKU is the model's code (no price, no quantity) and a child listing per article, varying by colour and/or size — the theme is chosen from what the Amazon product type declares. An article not yet on the store becomes a new child (action create); an article already sold there as a listing of its own — a model put on a store article by article, or copied from another store without its parent — is JOINED to the parent (action attach): only parentage_level, child_parent_sku_relationship and variation_theme are sent to it, by PATCH under the SKU Amazon knows it by (amazonSku when that differs), and its offer, photos and texts stay as they are. A listing Amazon already shows under this parent counts as in the family (skipped, listed). Every listing is first validated by Amazon (VALIDATION_PREVIEW); this tool only checks and creates nothing. Start from gaps: one entry per kind of problem with every SKU it concerns, found before Amazon is asked — size or color (set with update_product), price (none in the run's currency, the marketplace's: upsert_product_prices, set_product_channel_price or apply_bulk_price_change), productType (update_category), brand, images, condition, title; quantity with blocking=false: the article does not track stock, so the listing goes up without one (update_product with trackInventory, then adjust_stock); and barcodeLength with blocking=false: the article's barcode has another number of digits than the rest of the model, so a digit may be lost — confirm it from the label before publishing (update_product with ean). Amazon is asked only when no gap blocks. A listing that cannot be joined gets status excluded and holds nobody up — the rest of the model goes ahead, it stays a listing of its own, and every later run tries it again; the gap cannotAttach (blocking=false) lists them. Its reason is attachProblem — otherParent (on this store it is already a variation of another parent: never moved, settle it in Seller Central), productType (Amazon lists it under another specific product type than the family's category: fix the category's Amazon product type with update_category, or the listing in Seller Central) or notOnStore (the CRM records it on this store but Amazon has nothing under its SKU: refresh with inspect_amazon_listings refresh=true and check again — it then becomes a new child) — or, with no attachProblem, issues: Amazon's own dry run refused the join (a listing Amazon holds under its generic type PRODUCT is asked under the family's type and Amazon answers here). If Amazon refuses a join for a missing colour or size, fill them with update_amazon_listing_content parts ["attributes"]. Status blocked always comes with this article's own missing or issues; waiting means the article has nothing wrong and the run stopped on another article's gap or the model's blocker. Also returns parentSku, theme, currency, blocker (tooFewArticles, noAxis, missingAxisValue, duplicateCombination, themeUnsupported, parentSkuTaken, parentTitleTooLong, tooManyArticles — the last is this CRM's limit for one run, not Amazon's: never suggest splitting the model), fieldProblems (what the product type still needs per Amazon's schema, once per field: attribute key, title in the marketplace's language, kind missing or invalid, allowed values with labels, units, the SKUs concerned, and for an attribute made of several values its parts: each part's key attribute.part, title, required, allowed values and unresolved — true when neither a person nor the CRM has an answer for it), parentIssues, children per article (missing, quantity, barcode, Amazon's sentences, status; notChecked = Amazon did not get to it, call again — what passed is kept for an hour while the article's data stays the same, so each call only checks the rest) and skipped articles (already on Amazon, taken off the channel). The CRM fills model_name, list_price, the dimensions and a size attribute (from each article's own size, with its system and class) itself; set any other field, or a part reported as unresolved, with set_amazon_field_values on the model (every article inherits it) — keys and values from get_amazon_fields. Then create it with publish_amazon_variation_family.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id. Omit for the main store; for a write with several stores open it is required. Each store holds its own family, in its own language.

modelId.description: A product model id (the model a product's modelId points at; get_product shows it).

tools.name: publish_amazon_variation_family
tools.description: The model's active articles become ONE listing with variations on one Amazon store — Amazon's "variation family"; call it a model with variations when talking to the user: a parent whose SKU is the model's code (no price, no quantity) and a child listing per article, varying by colour and/or size — the theme is chosen from what the Amazon product type declares. An article not yet on the store becomes a new child (action create); an article already sold there as a listing of its own — a model put on a store article by article, or copied from another store without its parent — is JOINED to the parent (action attach): only parentage_level, child_parent_sku_relationship and variation_theme are sent to it, by PATCH under the SKU Amazon knows it by (amazonSku when that differs), and its offer, photos and texts stay as they are. A listing Amazon already shows under this parent counts as in the family (skipped, listed). Every listing is first validated by Amazon (VALIDATION_PREVIEW); only when ALL of them would be accepted is the family created — a REAL publication: the parent first, then each child with its price and quantity. Run check_amazon_variation_family first. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing, and while listing creation is not armed on the Amazon connection; joining listings already on the store changes live listings, so it is also refused (reason amazonContentPushDisarmed) while sending content to Amazon (contentPush) is not open for that store. Returns the same report with statuses created (a new child), attached (a listing joined to the parent), excluded (a listing left out, see check_amazon_variation_family), failed, notAttempted or notChecked; each child's offer names the price, currency, quantity and fulfilment it is submitted with (quantityOmitted says why no quantity goes out), and progress says what is left (createdNow, attachedNow, alreadyOnAmazon, remaining, notReached, excluded) and the one next step: done, callAgain, fixAndRetry, fixGaps or publish. A model of about 80 articles is meant to finish in one call; a bigger one, or a slow Amazon, takes more: notChecked and notAttempted both mean the run ran out of time, so call again — a dry run an article passed is kept for an hour while its data stays the same, created and joined articles are skipped (nothing is submitted twice), the parent and the theme stay, and the rest continue. created means Amazon ACCEPTED the child for processing, not that it is live: Amazon finishes asynchronously, so check the outcome with inspect_amazon_listings and never tell the user the family is live from this result alone. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id. Omit for the main store; for a write with several stores open it is required. Each store holds its own family, in its own language.

modelId.description: A product model id (the model a product's modelId points at; get_product shows it).

Changes nothing. Then send it with update_amazon_variation_parent.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id. Omit for the main store; for a write with several stores open it is required. Each store holds its own family, in its own language.

modelId.description: A product model id (the model a product's modelId points at; get_product shows it).

tools.name: update_amazon_variation_parent
tools.description: Send the parent of a model ALREADY on Amazon its title and selling points again — a REAL change on a live listing: the model's Amazon title and points (set_channel_texts with modelId), else its name in the marketplace's language. Replaces only item_name and bullet_point; nothing else a person set in Seller Central changes. Run check_amazon_variation_parent first. Refused until the owner switches on AI publishing, and while sending content to Amazon (contentPush) is not armed on the Amazon connection. Returns the same report with status sent, nothing or rejected. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id. Omit for the main store; for a write with several stores open it is required. Each store holds its own family, in its own language.
