tools.name: set_channel_texts
tools.description: Set the listing words of ONE product or ONE model for a channel — amazon (title up to 75 characters and up to 5 selling points) or ebay (title up to 80 characters, no points) — in the marketplace's language, which the CRM picks from the channel's marketplace (pass locale only when it says the channel sells in several languages). Which title a listing gets: the product's own words, else its model's title plus its colour or size («DEMI Borsa duffle 40 L, Blu»), else the product's name in that language. A model's title is also the title of Amazon's variation parent and of eBay's listing with variations — set it once per model instead of per colour. Write from the product's facts (get_product) and what the user said — never invent a claim. Saved in the CRM: new listings carry them; an existing Amazon offer gets them with update_amazon_listing_content parts ["texts"], an existing parent with update_amazon_variation_parent. title null with bulletPoints [] removes them; bulletPoints left out keeps the saved points. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

bulletPoints.description: Selling points in order; empty strings are dropped. Amazon shows up to 5 (500 characters each); eBay has none. Omit to keep the points already saved (changing only the title); [] removes them.

locale.description: The language the words are written in. Omit it: the CRM uses the channel's marketplace language (amazon.it → it). Needed only when the channel sells in several languages here (eBay on ebay.it and ebay.de, Amazon on amazon.it and amazon.de).

modelId.description: A product model id (get_product shows the model). Words set on the model go to every article of it without words of its own — as «model title, colour» — and are the title of Amazon's variation parent and of eBay's listing with variations. Give exactly one of productId or modelId.

platform.description: The channel the words are for: amazon (title up to 75 characters and selling points) or ebay (title up to 80 characters, no points).

productId.description: A product id returned by search_products — this article's own words, which win over its model's. Give exactly one of productId or modelId.

title.description: The title in the marketplace's language, within the channel's limit; null to fall back (an article to its model's title plus its colour or size, then its name; a model to its name in that language). null with bulletPoints [] removes the words.

tools.name: get_amazon_fields
tools.description: The fields of the Amazon product type of ONE product, model or category (name exactly one id), read from Amazon's own schema for the workspace's Amazon marketplace: each field's attribute key, its title in the marketplace's language, its kind (choice with Amazon's list of values and labels, number, measure with the units it accepts, text), whether the type requires it, the value set on this level (own) and the one it inherits from the model or the category (inherited), and — for a product, or a model read through its first active article — its status: missing or invalid (what Amazon would refuse) or filled, and fromCrm when the CRM already fills it from the product's characteristics or fields. fields lists in full the ones that are required, missing, refused or already hold a value; otherFields names every other field by key, title and kind — pass their keys in keys to get them in full. An attribute made of several values that only mean something together (a size: shirt_size, bottoms_size, footwear_size) appears as one field per part, keyed attribute.part (shirt_size.size_system); the article's own size part is listed only for a product. Fields the CRM always writes itself (title, brand, barcode, price, photos, the colour's name, the variation relationship) are never listed. The colour's name is the product's colour in the store's language (translations on get_product, written with upsert_product_translation); which of Amazon's colour families it belongs to is the field color.standardized_values, listed for a product only, which the CRM fills from the name unless a value is set here. Use it before set_amazon_field_values; for what a product still lacks to be listed, check_amazon_readiness. Read-only: it changes nothing.

categoryId.description: Read the fields of this CATEGORY's Amazon product type and the values set on it.

modelId.description: Read the fields for this MODEL — the values set on it and on its category, and what its first active article still misses.

productId.description: Read the fields for this one PRODUCT (article) — the values set on it, its model and its category, and what it still misses.

marketplaceId.description: The Amazon store whose product type, language and allowed values to use (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store.

keys.description: Attribute keys to return in full besides the ones that need attention — for a field listed under otherFields whose allowed values you need.

tools.name: set_amazon_field_values
tools.description: Set or remove values of Amazon product type fields on ONE product, model or category (name exactly one id) — the attributes Amazon requires that are not product facts the shop shows on its site or other channels (Reparto, Tipo di chiusura, Capacità). A category's value is the default of every product in it, a model's is shared by every colour and size, a product's overrides both. Keys and values come from get_amazon_fields: for a choice, one of its values (or labels); a number as digits; a measure with a unit it lists. An attribute made of several values is set part by part under attribute.part (shirt_size.size_system): a part's value must be on its list, and one answer on the model serves every article; the CRM builds a size from each article's own size, so only a part it reported as unresolved needs an answer. Every value is checked against Amazon's schema first, and the whole call is refused, naming the fields, when a key is not one a person fills or a value cannot be taken. Write only what the user stated or what the product's facts (get_product) establish, in the marketplace's language. Saved in the CRM only: a new listing carries them; an existing offer is not changed. null removes a value, so the level below shows through again. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

categoryId.description: Set the values on this CATEGORY — the default for every product in it.

modelId.description: Set the values on this MODEL — shared by every colour and size of it.

productId.description: Set the values on this one PRODUCT (article).

marketplaceId.description: The Amazon store whose product type, language and allowed values to use (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store.

key.description: The marketplace's attribute key (closure, department, number_of_compartments), or attribute.part for one part of an attribute made of several values (shirt_size.size_system) — get_amazon_fields lists them.

unit.description: For a measurement, the unit as the marketplace names it (liters, centimeters, kilograms) — one of the units get_amazon_fields lists for the field.

value.description: The value as a person writes it, in the marketplace's language: for a field with a list, one of its values or labels; a number as digits. null removes the value at this level.

values.description: The fields to set or remove, by Amazon attribute key. A value replaces what this level held; null removes it, so the model's or the category's value shows through again.

tools.name: list_economic_operators
tools.description: List the workspace's GPSR companies — the manufacturers and EU responsible persons marketplaces ask for (Amazon takes them as the EMAIL of a record the seller created in Seller Central). Each has id, name, email, phone, website and address. Assign them to a brand or supplier with assign_economic_operators; a product takes each role from its brand, else its supplier. Read-only.

tools.name: save_economic_operator
tools.description: Create a GPSR company (manufacturer or EU responsible person), or update one when id is given. The email is the key Amazon matches against the record in Seller Central, so it must be exactly that record's email — ask the user, never guess one. Name is unique in the workspace. Then assign it with assign_economic_operators. The result echoes the workspace.

company.description: name, email (required); phone, website, addressLine1, addressLine2, city, postalCode, stateOrProvince, country (two-letter code).

id.description: The company to update; omit to create one.

tools.name: assign_economic_operators
tools.description: Point a brand or a supplier at its GPSR companies: the manufacturer and the EU responsible person (ids from list_economic_operators, or null to clear). Every product of that brand takes them first, then the supplier's. Replaces both roles at once. The result echoes the workspace.

inputSchema.description: owner: { kind: brand | supplier, id }; manufacturerId and responsiblePersonId: a company id or null.

tools.name: list_amazon_shipping_templates
tools.description: List the seller's Amazon shipping templates on ONE store — each template's id (the value Amazon takes) and name (as typed in Seller Central), read from Amazon's seller-specific product type schema through any category mapped to a product type. Templates exist per store (amazon.de has its own). When Amazon names none for this seller, templates is empty and note says so: templates are created in Seller Central only (no API creates or edits them), and until one is assigned Amazon applies the account's default shipping settings. Needs a category mapped to an Amazon product type (update_category) and a listing marketplace on the Amazon connection; no arming. Read-only: it changes nothing. Then assign one with set_amazon_shipping; use get_amazon_fields for the other product type fields.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store. Templates exist per store.

tools.name: set_amazon_shipping
tools.description: Assign an Amazon shipping template and/or a handling time (the most days from order to dispatch, lead_time_to_ship_max_days) to ONE product, model or category (name exactly one id). Inherited like Amazon field values: a category's value is the default of every product in it, a model's is shared by every colour and size, a product's overrides both. The template is given by id or name from list_amazon_shipping_templates and is refused, with the available ones, when it is not one of that store's templates. The handling time is refused when the product type does not take it. null removes a value so the level below shows through; omit a field to leave it as it is. Saved in the CRM only: a new listing and an offer on an existing ASIN carry them, and update_amazon_listing_content with part shipping (dry run first with preview_amazon_listing_content) sends them to an offer already on Amazon, under the owner's content arming. With no template assigned nothing is sent and Amazon applies the account's default shipping settings; with no handling time Amazon keeps its own default. Merchant-fulfilled offers only — an FBA offer takes neither. Values are stored per language, so two stores sharing one (UK and Ireland) read the same template id and skip it where it is not listed; alsoReadBy names them. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

categoryId.description: Assign on this CATEGORY — the default for every product in it.

handlingDays.description: Handling time: the most days between the order and dispatch (lead_time_to_ship_max_days). null removes it so the level below shows through. Omit to leave it as it is. Amazon's dry run (preview_amazon_listing_content) judges the limit of the product type.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store. Templates exist per store.

modelId.description: Assign on this MODEL — shared by every colour and size of it.

templateId.description: The shipping template: its id or its name from list_amazon_shipping_templates. null removes it so the level below shows through. Omit to leave it as it is.

tools.name: bulk_set_product_brand
tools.description: Set — or clear — the BRAND of many products in one call, the way the CRM's product list bar does it. scope names the products: a list of ids (at most 100, from search_products), a model (every colour and size of it) or a category (add includeSubcategories to take the ones under it); an open filter is not accepted. A brand belongs to the model, so for a product in a model the model changes and every article of it follows — articles outside the ones named are counted in expandedByModel, never hidden. brandId comes from list_brands or create_brand (null clears the brand). Products that already have the brand are skipped. A brand called Unbranded needs no special handling: Amazon listings send it as Generic. Saved in the CRM; a live Amazon offer keeps its brand until it is updated there. Idempotent. Returns { affected, skipped, expandedByModel } and the workspace. Use update_product to change one product.

brandId.description: The brand id from list_brands, or null to remove the brand.

scope.description: Which products: { kind: 'ids', ids: [...] }, { kind: 'model', id } or { kind: 'category', id, includeSubcategories? }.

tools.name: set_amazon_field_values_for_products
tools.description: Set the SAME Amazon product type field values (item_form, number_of_items, unit_count, package dimensions …) on an explicit list of up to 25 products — set_amazon_field_values for each product, with the same checks against the Amazon schema of THAT product's type, so a product whose type does not take a key is refused for that key only. When every product shares the value, set it once on their model or category with set_amazon_field_values instead. Keys, kinds and allowed values come from get_amazon_fields (read it for one of the products). Saved in the CRM only: a new listing carries the values; an existing offer is not changed. null removes a value. Idempotent. Returns one result per product (saved, or the refusal naming the fields); products are independent, so some can succeed while others fail. The result echoes the workspace.

marketplaceId.description: The Amazon store whose product type, language and allowed values to use (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store.

productIds.description: The products to write, at most 25 ids.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

key.description: The marketplace's attribute key (closure, department, number_of_compartments), or attribute.part for one part of an attribute made of several values (shirt_size.size_system) — get_amazon_fields lists them.

unit.description: For a measurement, the unit as the marketplace names it (liters, centimeters, kilograms) — one of the units get_amazon_fields lists for the field.

value.description: The value as a person writes it, in the marketplace's language: for a field with a list, one of its values or labels; a number as digits. null removes the value at this level.

values.description: The fields to set or remove, by Amazon attribute key. A value replaces what this level held; null removes it, so the model's or the category's value shows through again.

tools.name: check_amazon_brand_access
tools.description: Ask Amazon whether this seller account may list a brand: allowed, approval_required (with the link to apply), not_eligible, or unknown. Amazon answers such questions per ASIN only (Listings Restrictions API) — there is no account-level brand query — so the answer is read for a SAMPLE ASIN of the brand: the one you pass, else the first catalog match whose brand equals the name. The result names the sampleAsin it was read for; when no item of the brand is found the status is unknown. Amazon has no 'application pending' state: until Amazon approves, the status stays approval_required. Reads Amazon, never writes. Use search_amazon_catalog to pick a sample ASIN, and check_amazon_readiness for a product.

brand.description: The brand name as Amazon shows it, e.g. 'DEMI Design Milano'.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id (APJ6JRA9NG5V4 is amazon.it, A1PA6795UKMFR9 is amazon.de). Omit for the main store.

sampleAsin.description: An ASIN of the brand on this store, when you already have one (from search_amazon_catalog).

tools.name: list_ebay_fulfillment_policies
tools.description: List the eBay shipping (fulfillment) business policies the seller has on each eBay site the connection sells on: fulfillmentPolicyId, name, freeShipping, shippingCost of the first domestic service (null for CALCULATED shipping), costType, handlingTime, domestic and international services, ship-to regions, and isDefault — the connection default. productCount is how many products chose the policy themselves; staleAssignments are product choices pointing at a policy eBay no longer has. Reads the stored copy; a site never read before is read from eBay, and refresh true reads eBay now. Reads only. Use a fulfillmentPolicyId from here with set_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy, bulk_set_ebay_fulfillment_policy or set_ebay_default_fulfillment_policy; for one product's policy use get_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy.

marketplaceId.description: An eBay MARKETPLACE id such as EBAY_IT. Omit it to list every marketplace the eBay connection sells on.

refresh.description: true reads the policies from eBay now instead of the stored copy. A marketplace never read before is read from eBay either way.

tools.name: sync_ebay_fulfillment_policies
tools.description: Re-read the eBay shipping (fulfillment) policies from eBay for every site the connection sells on, or one marketplaceId, and refresh the copy the CRM keeps — after the seller created, renamed or deleted a policy in Seller Hub. Returns the same shape as list_ebay_fulfillment_policies; check staleAssignments: products whose chosen policy eBay no longer has will be refused at their next draft or go-live until another policy is chosen. Changes no listing and no choice. Use list_ebay_fulfillment_policies for an ordinary read.

marketplaceId.description: An eBay MARKETPLACE id such as EBAY_IT. Omit it to refresh every marketplace the eBay connection sells on.

tools.name: get_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy
tools.description: Show ONE product's eBay shipping policy. Per eBay site: assignedPolicyId (the product's own choice, null when it has none), defaultPolicyId (the connection default) and effectivePolicyId with effectiveSource — product, connection_default or first_available — the policy a new draft or a go-live would carry, plus that site's policies. For a product with a draft or live listing it also reads the eBay offer live: offer.fulfillmentPolicyId is what buyers see now. Reads only. Use list_ebay_fulfillment_policies for the costs of every policy and get_ebay_offer_policies to read several products' offers at once.

productId.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: get_ebay_offer_policies
tools.description: Read the eBay offers of up to 25 products live and return, per offer, the fulfillment, payment and return policy ids it carries now, the shipping policy name, its eBay site and status (PUBLISHED = live, UNPUBLISHED = draft), and matchesAssignment — whether it carries the product's own choice in the CRM (null when the product has none). Products with no draft or live listing are listed in withoutOffer; notAttempted were not reached in the time budget — call again with those ids. Reads only. Use get_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy for one product's full picture.

productIds.description: The products whose eBay offers to read, at most 25 ids from search_products.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: set_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy
tools.description: Choose the eBay shipping (fulfillment) policy of ONE product, or with fulfillmentPolicyId null return it to the connection default. A product with no eBay listing stores the choice for its next draft. A draft or LIVE listing has its eBay offer updated in place — no relisting — when listing writes are armed on the eBay connection, and the offer is then read back to confirm; with listing writes off a live listing is refused and a draft stores the choice for go-live. Per-service shipping cost overrides tied to the old policy are removed (droppedShippingCostOverrides). Returns productId, sku, offerId, marketplaceId, previousFulfillmentPolicyId, newFulfillmentPolicyId, status (updated, unchanged, saved, unverified, failed), verified and error — tell the user a listing changed only when status is updated. Refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

fulfillmentPolicyId.description: A fulfillmentPolicyId from list_ebay_fulfillment_policies, for the same marketplace. null removes the product's own choice so the connection default (then eBay's first policy) applies.

marketplaceId.description: An eBay MARKETPLACE id such as EBAY_IT — never the eBay connection id. Omit it when the eBay connection sells on one site; the server uses that one. Required when the connection sells on several, unless the product already has an eBay offer (its own site is then used).

productId.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: bulk_set_ebay_fulfillment_policy
tools.description: Choose one eBay shipping (fulfillment) policy — or null for the connection default — for up to 25 products on one eBay site, with the same per-product rules as set_product_ebay_fulfillment_policy: no listing stores the choice; a draft or live listing has its offer updated in place and read back. The policy is checked against eBay once before any product is touched, and a product whose listing lives on another eBay site fails with marketplaceMismatch instead of being moved. Returns results per product (status updated, unchanged, saved, unverified or failed with the eBay error), counts and notAttempted (not reached in the time budget — call again with those ids). Refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

fulfillmentPolicyId.description: A fulfillmentPolicyId from list_ebay_fulfillment_policies, for the same marketplace. null removes the product's own choice so the connection default (then eBay's first policy) applies.

marketplaceId.description: The eBay MARKETPLACE id the policy belongs to, such as EBAY_IT. Omit it when the eBay connection sells on one site. A product whose eBay offer lives on another site is reported as failed, never moved.

productIds.description: The products to change, at most 25 ids from search_products.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: set_ebay_default_fulfillment_policy
tools.description: Set the eBay connection's default shipping (fulfillment) policy for one eBay site, or null to remove it. Products without their own choice carry it in every new draft and when a draft goes live; LIVE listings keep the policy they have — change those with bulk_set_ebay_fulfillment_policy. The policy is checked against eBay's live list first; with no default, listings use the first policy eBay returns. Returns marketplaceId, previousFulfillmentPolicyId, fulfillmentPolicyId and the policy. Refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

fulfillmentPolicyId.description: A fulfillmentPolicyId from list_ebay_fulfillment_policies, for the same marketplace. null removes the default: listings without their own choice then use the first policy eBay returns.

marketplaceId.description: An eBay MARKETPLACE id such as EBAY_IT. Omit it when the eBay connection sells on one site.

tools.name: get_ebay_variation_listing
tools.description: Show a product MODEL as one eBay multi-variation listing: state (none, draft, live), marketplaceId, listingId and listingUrl, the stable groupKey, and every article of the model with its sku, colour, size, channelState on eBay and inclusion — included, not_active, not_on_channel (put it on the channel with set_channel_membership) or single_listing (it has its own eBay draft or listing, which must be deleted or ended first). Also says whether eBay is connected and whether the owner armed listing creation. Reads the CRM only. Use inspect_ebay_variation_listing for eBay's own checks before saving.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

tools.name: inspect_ebay_variation_listing
tools.description: Run every check saving a model's eBay multi-variation listing would run, writing nothing: each article's required fields and price in the marketplace currency, the variation axes (colour and/or size, named as the eBay site names them), duplicate or missing variation values, the category (suggested from the title, or the saved listing's), whether it allows variations, item condition, required item specifics, one shipping policy for all articles, business policies and inventory location. Returns ready, marketplaceId, categoryId, axes, variationCount and issues (reason, message, skus). Needs a marketplace but not the owner's arming. Reads eBay. Use save_ebay_variation_listing once ready is true.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

marketplaceId.description: eBay marketplace id (EBAY_IT, EBAY_DE…) for a FIRST save, when the connection sells on several. A saved listing keeps its marketplace; omit it then.

tools.name: save_ebay_variation_listing
tools.description: Save a product model on eBay as ONE listing with variations — every active article of the model on the eBay channel is a variation (its own SKU, price and stock; buyers choose colour and size). Writes the inventory items, the inventory item group and each variation's offer; a draft stays unpublished. When the listing is already LIVE this updates it in place: new variations, prices and texts reach buyers at once, and articles that no longer qualify leave it. Returns status: blocked (with issues — reason, message, skus — and nothing written), saved (a draft on eBay) or published, plus marketplaceId, listingId, listingUrl, publishedAt, variationCount, failed (variations eBay refused, by sku — nothing is published while any) and removedSkus (articles that left the listing). A partial/uncertain publication returns reason ebayVariationReconciliationPending with retryable=true. Retry the same operation to check eBay first; never withdraw or delete to repair it. Confirmed recovery updates CRM links without publishing again. Needs listing creation armed on the eBay connection, and is refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

marketplaceId.description: eBay marketplace id (EBAY_IT, EBAY_DE…) for a FIRST save, when the connection sells on several. A saved listing keeps its marketplace; omit it then.

tools.name: publish_ebay_variation_listing
tools.description: Publish a product model on eBay as ONE live listing with variations: saves it first exactly like save_ebay_variation_listing (so eBay gets the articles as they are now), then publishes the whole group — a real listing buyers can purchase. Returns status: blocked (with issues — reason, message, skus — and nothing written), saved (a draft on eBay) or published, plus marketplaceId, listingId, listingUrl, publishedAt, variationCount, failed (variations eBay refused, by sku — nothing is published while any) and removedSkus (articles that left the listing). A partial/uncertain publication returns reason ebayVariationReconciliationPending with retryable=true. Retry the same operation to check eBay first; never withdraw or delete to repair it. Confirmed recovery updates CRM links without publishing again. Needs listing creation armed on the eBay connection, and is refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Confirm with the user before calling. The result echoes the workspace.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

marketplaceId.description: eBay marketplace id (EBAY_IT, EBAY_DE…) for a FIRST save, when the connection sells on several. A saved listing keeps its marketplace; omit it then.

tools.name: withdraw_ebay_variation_listing
tools.description: End a model's LIVE eBay multi-variation listing: every variation leaves sale at once. The group and its offers stay on eBay as a draft, so publish_ebay_variation_listing restores the same listing. Works while listing creation is disarmed (a way off eBay is never locked), but is refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Returns withdrawn. The result echoes the workspace.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

tools.name: delete_ebay_variation_draft
tools.description: Delete a model's UNPUBLISHED eBay multi-variation draft: every variation's offer and the inventory item group are removed from eBay; the articles stay on the channel, ready for a new listing (together or one by one). A live listing is refused — end it with withdraw_ebay_variation_listing first. Refused until the workspace owner switches on AI publishing. Returns deleted. The result echoes the workspace.

model.description: The product model: its code — the productGroupId get_product and search_products return for every article of it — or its id. Its active articles on the eBay channel become the listing's variations.

tools.name: list_content_channels
tools.description: List the social channels this workspace can publish posts to — Telegram channel, Instagram, Facebook page, LinkedIn, Threads, Viber channel — with, per channel, whether it is ready, where it posts (destination), its public address (profile: profileUrl, publicFeedUrl — a public Telegram channel reads without signing in at t.me/s/<name>, older posts via ?before=<post id> — and readableBy: anyone, login_required or not_public), its text limit (maxTextLength) and, when not ready, the setup step the person must do in Obriym. Open the profile with your own browsing to read every post the channel already has, including ones written outside Obriym. Also returns now (the current time on the workspace's clock) and the workspace time zone — build schedule_content_post times from them — the image rules, and publishingEnabled: whether the workspace owner allows AI clients to publish or schedule. Read-only. Call it before create_content_post and only target ready channels.

tools.name: list_content_posts
tools.description: List the workspace's social posts, newest first, 20 per page: id, working title, status (draft, scheduled, publishing, published, partial, failed), channels, scheduled and published times. Filter by status or by part of the title. Read-only. Use get_content_post for one post's texts and per-channel results; use it to check what is already scheduled before planning more posts.

page.description: Page number, 20 publications per page, newest first.

query.description: Part of a publication's working title.

status.description: Only publications in this state: draft, scheduled, publishing, published, partial (some channels failed) or failed.

tools.name: list_published_posts
tools.description: List what this workspace has already published to its social channels, newest first: per post the exact text each channel got (hashtags included), the channel, permalink, publishedAt, title, contentPostId and productId, plus per channel the publishing rhythm (lastPostedAt, postsLast7Days, postsLast30Days, medianGapHours, nextScheduledAt, scheduledCount) and, in sources, the channel's public address (profileUrl, publicFeedUrl) with a note. Only posts published through Obriym are listed. Posts typed directly into the network are not stored here — before planning, compare against BOTH this list and the channel itself: open sources[].publicFeedUrl or profileUrl with your own browsing to read everything posted there (a public Telegram channel reads at t.me/s/<name>; LinkedIn and Instagram may need a login; a Viber channel is read in the Viber app; a private channel cannot be read from outside). Never claim the channel had no other posts, and say so when a channel cannot be read. Use it before planning or writing new posts: avoid repeating a topic, product or phrasing, and use the rhythm to choose dates that keep a steady flow; then create_content_post and schedule_content_post. Filter by channel or by days (YYYY-MM-DD on the workspace's clock), 20 per page. Read-only. Use list_content_posts for drafts and scheduled posts, get_content_post for one post's per-channel results.

channel.description: Only this network's posts: instagram, facebook, telegram, linkedin, threads or viber. Omit for all channels.

from.description: First day to include, YYYY-MM-DD, a calendar day on the workspace's clock. Omit for no lower bound.

page.description: Page number, newest posts first. Default 1.

to.description: Last day to include, YYYY-MM-DD, inclusive, on the workspace's clock. Omit for no upper bound.

tools.name: get_content_post
tools.description: Read one social post: its main text, hashtags, images, linked product, status and schedule, and per channel the text that channel gets (ownText or the main text), its length against the channel limit, whether the channel is ready, and what publishing returned there — status, link to the live post (permalink) or the network's error. Read-only. Use list_content_posts to find the id; call it after publish_content_post to report the links.

id.description: The publication id returned by create_content_post or list_content_posts.

tools.name: create_content_post
tools.description: Create a social post as a DRAFT — nothing is published. Give it a working title, the main text, optional hashtags, the channels (each may carry its own text), and images: public https image links (Obriym stores its own copy), files the person attached in ChatGPT (the `files` field, filled by ChatGPT), links returned by create_image_upload for local files, and/or a catalog product whose photos are attached and whose sell-out later marks the live Telegram and Threads post as sold. Each channel's text, with hashtags, must fit that channel's limit (list_content_channels). Returns the post id and warnings — a channel that is not ready, Instagram without an image — to relay to the person. Not idempotent: each call creates a new draft. Then use schedule_content_post or publish_content_post. Echoes the workspace.

channel.description: A social channel: telegram (the bound Telegram channel), instagram, facebook (the Facebook page), linkedin, threads or viber (the connected Viber channel). Use only channels list_content_channels reports as ready.

text.description: Text written for THIS network only. Omit it to publish the post's main text. It must fit the channel's maxTextLength from list_content_channels together with the hashtags (Threads allows 500 characters, Instagram 2200).

channels.description: Where the post goes — one entry per channel, each at most once. Every channel publishes the main text unless its entry carries its own text.

format.description: post = a regular feed post; story = an Instagram/Facebook story, which needs an image. Defaults to post.

hashtags.description: Hashtags without the "#" sign, at most 30. They are appended to every channel's text as their own line.

imageUrls.description: Images to attach, as public https links to JPEG, PNG or WebP files of at most 2 MB each. Obriym downloads and keeps its own copy, so the link only has to work now. Threads accepts JPEG and PNG only.

items.description: A public https link to the image file itself.

productId.description: A catalog product this post advertises (id from search_products). Links the post to the product, so when it sells out Obriym marks the live Telegram and Threads post as sold, and lets productPhotos attach the product's photos.

productPhotos.description: With productId: attach the product's own photos after any imageUrls, up to 10 images in total. Set false to post without them.

text.description: The post's main text, in the language the audience reads. Plain text: no markdown, links are written out in full. Never invent a price, discount, stock level or date — state only facts the user or the CRM gave you.

title.description: An internal working title shown in Obriym's Publications list, e.g. "Monday — new arrivals". Never published.

files.description: Image files the person attached in ChatGPT. ChatGPT fills this field itself; any other client leaves it out and passes image links instead (or uploads files with create_image_upload).

download_url.description: Temporary link ChatGPT gives to the attached file.

file_id.description: ChatGPT's id of the attached file.

tools.name: update_content_post
tools.description: Change a draft or scheduled post: working title, main text, hashtags, format, or its channels and their own texts (sending channels replaces the whole set). Fields you omit stay as they are; images cannot be changed here. Refused for a published post — a post already live on a network cannot be changed from Obriym; create a new one instead. Refused while the post is being published. Repeating the same call changes nothing further. Echoes the workspace.

channels.description: Replaces the post's channels and their texts. Omit to keep them as they are.

channel.description: A social channel: telegram (the bound Telegram channel), instagram, facebook (the Facebook page), linkedin, threads or viber (the connected Viber channel). Use only channels list_content_channels reports as ready.

text.description: Text written for THIS network only. Omit it to publish the post's main text. It must fit the channel's maxTextLength from list_content_channels together with the hashtags (Threads allows 500 characters, Instagram 2200).

format.description: post = a regular feed post; story = an Instagram/Facebook story, which needs an image. Defaults to post.

hashtags.description: Replaces the hashtags, without the "#" sign. Omit to keep them; [] removes them.

id.description: The publication id returned by create_content_post or list_content_posts.

title.description: An internal working title shown in Obriym's Publications list, e.g. "Monday — new arrivals". Never published.

tools.name: delete_content_post
tools.description: Delete a post that has not been published — a draft, a scheduled post (its schedule goes with it) or one whose every channel failed. Its own stored images are deleted too; a linked product's photos are never touched. Refused for a post that went out on any channel: that record stays. This cannot be undone. Echoes the workspace.

id.description: The publication id returned by create_content_post or list_content_posts.

tools.name: schedule_content_post
tools.description: Schedule a post to be published at a time, or cancel its schedule. Obriym itself publishes it to every ready channel of the post within about 15 minutes after that time — the AI client does not need to be running then. This is how regular publishing is set up: create several drafts, then schedule each. Needs the owner's "AI may publish to social channels" switch to schedule (see publishingEnabled in list_content_channels); cancelling (scheduledAt: null) does not. A post that is published or being published cannot be scheduled. Returns a warning when no channel of the post is ready yet. Echoes the workspace.

id.description: The publication id returned by create_content_post or list_content_posts.

scheduledAt.description: When to publish, as an ISO 8601 date-time WITH its time-zone offset, e.g. "2026-10-12T10:00:00+03:00". At least one minute and at most one year ahead; list_content_channels returns the workspace time zone. Obriym publishes it itself at that time — no AI client needs to be running. null cancels the schedule and returns the post to a draft.

tools.name: publish_content_post
tools.description: Publish a post NOW to every ready channel of it — a real, public post in the business's name that followers see at once and that cannot be taken back from Obriym. A channel already published is never sent twice, so calling it again only retries the channels that failed or were not ready. Returns, per channel, the outcome (published, failed, already_published, skipped_not_configured with the setup step, skipped_empty, skipped_unsupported), the link to the live post and the network's error. Needs the owner's "AI may publish to social channels" switch (publishingEnabled in list_content_channels). Confirm with the person before calling it unless they asked for the publication outright. Echoes the workspace.

id.description: The publication id returned by create_content_post or list_content_posts.

tools.name: list_suppliers
tools.description: List the workspace's suppliers: id, name, status (active or archived), the currency they invoice in and how many products each covers (productCount). Read-only. Use it as the id source for a {kind:'supplier'} scope of preview_bulk_price_change and apply_bulk_price_change — 'raise every Sipec product by 5%'. Categories, brands and warehouses come from list_categories, list_brands and list_warehouses.

tools.name: get_product_pricing
tools.description: Everything about ONE product's prices in one call: its own price, old price and currency; the price-list rows (other currencies); per-channel price overrides (platform, currency, price); the channel price rules that apply where there is no override (channelPriceRules); wholesale quantity breaks per currency; the purchase cost with its currency (a bundle's cost is derived from its components and cannot be set on it); and the markup over cost per sale currency (marginPercent = price ÷ cost − 1, in percent; not a margin on the price) — the cost crossed at the workspace's stated rate, null with missingRate true when no rate is stated. Read-only. Use search_products for the id; call it before set_product_channel_price, set_product_price_tiers or upsert_product_prices so you change the right row, and after a change to confirm it. For a whole group of products use preview_bulk_price_change.

id.description: The product id returned by search_products or get_product — never a SKU or a name.

tools.name: preview_bulk_price_change
tools.description: Dry run of a bulk price change — step 1 of 2; nothing is written. Give a rule (percent, fixed, fromCost, discount, endDiscount, compareAtMarkup, compareAtClear), a scope (a named category, brand, supplier, warehouse or model, or up to 100 explicit product ids) and optionally a target (the product's price, a price-list currency, or the purchase cost). Returns totalItems (how many products would change), a sample of up to 10 with from/to, old price and cost, belowCost (how many would sell below their cost), skipped grouped by reason (no price, no cost, no rate, unchanged, …), the currency, and a digest. Always show the person the counts, the sample, the skipped reasons and any belowCost warning BEFORE applying. Then call apply_bulk_price_change with the SAME rule, scope and target and this digest. Ids come from list_categories, list_brands, list_suppliers, list_warehouses (a category includes its sub-categories only with includeSubcategories) and search_products. Read-only and repeatable.

tools.name: list_channel_price_rules
tools.description: List how each connected sales channel prices products, one row per channel and currency: rule null means the base price, otherwise percent, fixed and rounding are added to it. The currency null means the channel has not told the CRM its currency yet. Read-only. Use preview_channel_price_rule to see what a change would do, and get_product_pricing for one product.

platform.description: One sales channel, e.g. ebay. Omit for every connected one.

tools.name: preview_channel_price_rule
tools.description: Dry run of a price rule for one sales channel in one currency, step 1 of 2; nothing is written. A rule prices every product on the channel from its base price (price + percent, then + fixed, then rounding) and moves with the base price; a product with its own price on the channel keeps that price. Pass rule null to go back to the base price. Returns how many products would change, how many have their own price, how many have no price in that currency, how many would sell below cost, sample rows before and after, and the digest set_channel_price_rule needs. Show the person this result before saving. Advertising channels (Google Merchant) cannot have a rule.

currency.description: The currency the rule applies in. list_channel_price_rules names the currencies each connected channel sells in.

platform.description: The sales channel, e.g. ebay or amazon.

fixed.description: Amount added to the base price after the percent, in the rule's currency. 0 for none.

percent.description: Percent added to the base price: 15 sells at base + 15%. Negative lowers it, down to -50. 0 for none.

rounding.description: How the result is rounded: cents (to the cent), whole (up to a whole number), nine (up to a whole number ending in 9), tens (up to tens), ninety_nine (ending in .99).

rule.description: The rule to check. null removes it: the base price again.

tools.name: set_channel_price_rule
tools.description: Save a price rule for one sales channel in one currency, step 2 of 2, after preview_channel_price_rule. Send the SAME platform, currency and rule with that preview's digest; a digest from an older preview is refused. Applies to every product on the channel on its next update, wherever the owner has turned price updates on, and to new listings; it never turns price updates on. Requires the workspace owner's switch for bulk price changes in Settings → Integrations → Connect AI, which is off by default. rule null removes the rule. Idempotent. The result echoes the workspace.

currency.description: The currency the rule applies in. list_channel_price_rules names the currencies each connected channel sells in.

platform.description: The sales channel, e.g. ebay or amazon.

fixed.description: Amount added to the base price after the percent, in the rule's currency. 0 for none.

tools.name: set_product_channel_price
tools.description: Set — or clear — the price ONE sales channel gets for ONE product, instead of the product's ordinary price in that currency. Send price as a decimal string to set it (with an optional compareAtPrice, the old price, higher than price) or price null to remove the override so the channel gets the ordinary price again. Per platform and currency: Prom, Rozetka, eBay, Amazon, Shopify, WooCommerce, OLX or Google Merchant. Send only an amount the person stated. The new price reaches the channel the same way a price edit does — only where the owner armed price writes; on Amazon a price goes out only with the hourly push or sync_amazon_offers (pass the changed productIds to send them now). This is not the price-list row for a currency (upsert_product_prices). Idempotent; clearing a missing override is not an error. Returns { changed }. Read get_product_pricing first. Echoes the workspace.

compareAtPrice.description: The old (struck-through) price on this channel, higher than price; omit or null for none. Ignored when price is null.

currency.description: The currency the channel sells in (uppercase 3-letter ISO code). get_product_pricing and the channel's readiness show which currency a channel uses.

id.description: The product id returned by search_products or get_product — never a SKU or a name.

platform.description: The sales channel this price is for: prom, rozetka, woocommerce, shopify, olx, amazon, ebay or google_merchant.

price.description: The price this ONE channel gets, instead of the product's ordinary price in that currency, as a decimal string above zero. null removes the override — the channel then gets the ordinary price again. Send only an amount the person stated; never a converted or guessed value.

tools.name: set_product_price_tiers
tools.description: Replace ONE product's wholesale quantity breaks in ONE currency — 'from 12 units, 12.40 each'. The list you send becomes the whole set for that currency (at most 10; each quantity at least 2 and once; a bigger quantity must cost less per unit); an empty list removes all its breaks. The product must already be priced in that currency. Breaks apply to buyers outside the team (the customer portal and connected partners), never to the website or marketplaces, and the buyer gets the better of a break or their own discount. Idempotent. Returns { count }. Read get_product_pricing first. Echoes the workspace.

currency.description: The currency of these breaks (uppercase 3-letter ISO code). The product must already be priced in it — its own currency or a price-list row.

id.description: The product id returned by search_products or get_product — never a SKU or a name.

minQuantity.description: From this many units. At least 2 — the price for one unit is the product's own price.

price.description: The price PER UNIT from that quantity, as a decimal string. Must be lower than the price of every smaller break.

tiers.description: The wholesale breaks for that currency, at most 10. This list REPLACES the product's breaks in that currency; an empty list removes them all. Each quantity once, and a bigger quantity always costs less per unit.

tools.name: get_channel_stock_limit
tools.description: Read the global or product-specific maximum published quantity on one numeric-inventory channel. Optional productId returns mode (inherit/limit/unlimited), own and effective ceiling, delivery state and reasons; readiness reports disabled inventory writes across all nine numeric-stock channels. Delivery items include target scope, attempted quantity, reasons and optional import reference; submitted means asynchronous processing, not confirmed live stock. maxQuantity null means unlimited. Each tracked SKU publishes min(available after reservations, maxQuantity); this does not reserve stock. Read-only. Use preview_channel_stock_limit before changing or removing it.

productId.description: Optional product/SKU id from search_products. Omit to change the global channel rule.

tools.name: preview_channel_stock_limit
tools.description: Dry run of a channel's maximum published quantity per SKU; nothing is written or sent. Optional productId targets ONE SKU: inherit true with maxQuantity null restores the channel rule; otherwise positive maxQuantity overrides it and null explicitly means unlimited. Without productId, positive maxQuantity sets the global ceiling and null removes it. Returns product counts (total, changed, untracked, paused), a truncation flag, before/after sample quantities and a signed previewToken valid for 15 minutes. Show the person these numbers, then use set_channel_stock_limit with the SAME platform, maxQuantity and token. Physical stock and stock-write permissions stay unchanged.

productId.description: Optional product/SKU id from search_products. Omit to change the global channel rule.

inherit.description: Product only: true restores the channel rule (send maxQuantity null). Otherwise maxQuantity null explicitly bypasses the channel ceiling for this SKU.

maxQuantity.description: Maximum published quantity per SKU on this channel. Positive integer; null removes the ceiling. Availability after reservations remains the upper bound. Never changes physical stock.

tools.name: set_channel_stock_limit
tools.description: Save or remove a channel's maximum published quantity per SKU after preview_channel_stock_limit. Send the SAME platform, optional productId, inherit and maxQuantity (product inherit true restores the channel rule; product null without inherit explicitly bypasses it), with that preview's token copied verbatim. A stale, expired or mismatched preview is refused: preview again and show the new result. Requires settings:write (owner/admin over OAuth or an explicitly scoped token) AND the workspace owner's AI marketplace-writes switch, off by default. Saves the rule, audits it, expires caches and schedules bounded stock delivery to this channel; remaining products reconcile through scheduled sync. A no-op queues no new delivery; use retry_channel_stock_delivery for a resend. Never changes physical stock, channel membership, paused products or armed write directions. Confirm with the person after showing the preview. Echoes the workspace.

productId.description: Optional product/SKU id from search_products. Omit to change the global channel rule.

inherit.description: Product only: true restores the channel rule (send maxQuantity null). Otherwise maxQuantity null explicitly bypasses the channel ceiling for this SKU.

maxQuantity.description: Maximum published quantity per SKU on this channel. Positive integer; null removes the ceiling. Availability after reservations remains the upper bound. Never changes physical stock.

previewToken.description: Copy verbatim from preview_channel_stock_limit for the SAME workspace, platform and maxQuantity. Expires after 15 minutes; preview again after a conflict.

tools.name: retry_channel_stock_delivery
tools.description: Retry the current saved stock policy for a channel or optional productId, without changing the rule or arming any direction. Read get_channel_stock_limit first, copy its current retryToken verbatim, and show its delivery/readiness reasons; disabled inventory writes stay disabled. Requires settings:write and the owner's AI marketplace-writes switch. Queues up to 500 eligible products; remaining products use scheduled reconciliation. A queued job is not marketplace acceptance. Confirm with the person first. Echoes the workspace.

retryToken.description: Copy the current retryToken from get_channel_stock_limit for the same workspace, platform and optional productId. Expires in 15 minutes.

tools.name: preview_channel_warehouses
tools.description: Dry run of the warehouses one marketplace sells from; nothing is written or sent. The channel would publish each tracked product's units on these warehouses minus the units open orders hold there (a bundle: whole bundles its components there can make), and its orders would take units from them in this order. Returns total and changed product counts, paused products, a truncation flag, before/after samples and a signed previewToken valid for 15 minutes. Refused when the workspace keeps one count per product. Read get_stock_sources and list_warehouses first; show the person these numbers, then call set_channel_warehouses with the SAME platform, warehouseIds and token.

platform.description: The marketplace slug from list_marketplaces whose warehouses change; get_stock_sources lists the channels that take a list.

warehouseIds.description: The warehouses the channel sells from, in the order its orders take units: own warehouses or supplier showcases (kind own or supplier in list_warehouses), each once, at most 20. null removes the list, so the channel publishes each product's total again.

tools.name: set_channel_warehouses
tools.description: Save the warehouses one marketplace sells from, after preview_channel_warehouses: send the SAME platform and warehouseIds with that preview's token copied verbatim; a stale, expired or mismatched preview, or a list changed meanwhile, is refused — preview again. Requires settings:write (owner/admin over OAuth or an explicitly scoped token) AND the workspace owner's AI marketplace-writes switch, off by default. Saves and audits the list and queues delivery of the new quantities to the channel at once (Google Merchant takes them at its next run); saving the same list changes nothing. Never moves physical stock, channel membership or armed write directions. Confirm with the person after showing the preview. Echoes the workspace.

platform.description: The marketplace slug from list_marketplaces whose warehouses change; get_stock_sources lists the channels that take a list.

warehouseIds.description: The warehouses the channel sells from, in the order its orders take units: own warehouses or supplier showcases (kind own or supplier in list_warehouses), each once, at most 20. null removes the list, so the channel publishes each product's total again.

previewToken.description: The previewToken returned by preview_channel_warehouses for the SAME platform and warehouseIds, copied verbatim.

tools.name: set_order_warehouses
tools.description: Save the warehouses an order takes its units from when its channel has no list of its own — orders made in the CRM, the customer portal, the shop's site API and channels without a list — in order of use; a shortage goes to the first warehouse that may go below zero. Send expected as get_stock_sources returned orders.warehouseIds; a list changed meanwhile is refused — read again. null removes the list (each product's primary warehouse again). Requires settings:write (owner/admin over OAuth or an explicitly scoped token). Applies to deductions from now on: no stock moves, nothing is sent to a marketplace, a line already deducted or placed by hand stays. Audited; saving the same list changes nothing. tools.name: create_image_upload
tools.description: Get one-time links for uploading image FILES from the agent's own machine — for clients that can read local files and send HTTP requests (Claude Code, Cursor, scripts). A chat client passes image links instead, and ChatGPT passes attached files itself through the files field. For each link, send the raw file bytes with HTTP PUT within 15 minutes — for example: curl -X PUT --data-binary @photo.jpg "<uploadUrl>". One file per link; JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 2 MB each (a bigger file is refused — there is no resize). The PUT answers JSON with url: pass that url to add_product_images (images[].url), create_content_post (imageUrls), set_category_image or set_brand_image (url), which store their own copy. Creating links changes nothing in the CRM. Returns { uploads: [{ uploadUrl, expiresAt }], maxBytes, allowedTypes }. Needs products:write or content:write.

count.description: How many upload links to create — one per file, at most 10.

tools.name: add_product_images
tools.description: Add photos to ONE product, after the photos it already has: public https image links (images, each with an optional caption), files the person attached in ChatGPT (files — ChatGPT fills it), or links returned by create_image_upload for files on the agent's own machine. Obriym downloads every image and stores its OWN COPY in the workspace's storage — the link may be temporary and nothing hotlinks to it. Limits: JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 2 MB each (a bigger file is refused — there is no resize), at most 10 photos per product. All or nothing: if any link fails, or the total would exceed 10, nothing is stored and the reason is returned. Saves through the product form's own operation (version check, audit, channel updates). Not idempotent: repeating the call adds the photos again. Returns the product's full photo list { url, alt } — the first is the main photo. Use get_product first to see the current photos and update_product_images to reorder, caption or remove them. The result echoes the workspace.

alt.description: Caption (alt text) of the photo, up to 200 characters. Empty or omitted: the storefront falls back to the product name. Do not invent a description of what you cannot see.

url.description: A public https image link (JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 2 MB). Obriym downloads it and stores its own copy in the workspace, so the link may be temporary.

images.description: Photos to ADD after the product's current ones, in order. The product may hold at most 10 photos in total; a request that would exceed it is refused and nothing is stored.

productId.description: The product id from search_products or get_product.

files.description: Image files the person attached in ChatGPT. ChatGPT fills this field itself; any other client leaves it out and passes image links instead (or uploads files with create_image_upload).

download_url.description: Temporary link ChatGPT gives to the attached file.

file_id.description: ChatGPT's id of the attached file.

tools.name: update_product_images

Returns the new list and how many were removed. It never adds photos: every url must already belong to the product, otherwise the call is refused and nothing changes — use add_product_images to add. Idempotent: the same call twice leaves the same result. Saves through the product form's own operation. Call get_product first and copy the urls exactly. The result echoes the workspace.

images.description: The product's photos as they should be AFTER the change: the order given becomes the display order (the first is the main photo) and each alt replaces the stored caption (empty clears it). Every url must already belong to the product — to add a photo use add_product_images.

productId.description: The product id from search_products or get_product.

Pass url: null to remove the current picture. Idempotent in effect: repeating it leaves the same picture. Use list_categories to find the category id. The result echoes the workspace.

tools.description: Stop the workspace's bulk AI translation. Products already translated keep their text, and no further credits are spent. Idempotent: with nothing running it changes nothing. The result echoes the workspace.

tools.name: list_content_locales
tools.description: List the languages this workspace writes product content in: the base language (the text stored on products, categories and brands themselves), the extra languages the owner added, and the offered set — every language the CRM shows as a translation tab. Call it BEFORE writing any translation (upsert_product_translation, upsert_category_translation, upsert_brand_translation) and write only offered languages; never write the base language as a translation.

tools.name: upsert_category_translation
tools.description: Set a category's name and/or description in ONE language, leaving every other language as it is. Translate the text yourself — Obriym does not translate for MCP clients. Call list_content_locales first; the workspace's base language is refused (use update_category for it). A language needs a translated name before it can hold a description; description null clears it. tools.name: preview_google_merchant_products
tools.description: Show, for 1 to 25 products, the exact body the Google Merchant push would send for each one — title, description, link, image links, price, availability, identifiers and custom labels — or the reason it would be held back (blocker: no_url, no_title, no_price, no_image, no_translation, not_shoppable, no_feed_label). It walks the same collect step and the same builder as the real push, so it cannot differ from what Google would receive. Local and read-only: no Google call, nothing is sent or stored, and it needs no arming. A product that is not an active, unpaused member of the Google channel is listed in notOnChannel (set_channel_membership adds it). Returns { adapterId, adapterName, feedLabel, currency, contentLanguage, items, notOnChannel }. Use check_channel_readiness for the whole channel's blockers and push_google_merchant_catalog to actually send; fix a blocker with update_product, upsert_product_prices or upsert_product_translation and preview again.

adapterId.description: The Google Merchant connection id from list_marketplaces / get_marketplace. Omit it when the workspace has exactly one connection; with several, omitting it is refused and names them.

productIds.description: The products to preview, at most 25 ids from search_products.

items.description: A product id returned by search_products.

tools.name: get_google_merchant_product_performance
tools.description: Clicks and impressions per product in Google Shopping for a date range, best first, read from Google's Merchant API Reports on demand — nothing is stored, so it is a question, not a sync. Each row has offerId, title, clicks, impressions and clickThroughRate. At most 92 days per call and 100 products; truncated is true when more products matched than limit, so narrow the dates or raise limit. Conversions are not included. Read-only: it changes nothing at Google and needs no arming, only a connected Google account. Use get_marketplace for what Google decided about the products (moderation), and list_ad_campaigns for spend and the sales the CRM recorded.

adapterId.description: The Google Merchant connection id from list_marketplaces / get_marketplace. Omit it when the workspace has exactly one connection; with several, omitting it is refused and names them.

from.description: First day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive).

limit.description: How many products to return, best first. Default 25, at most 100.

to.description: Last day of the range, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). The range is at most 92 days.

tools.name: set_google_merchant_labels
tools.description: Set or clear Google's custom labels customLabel1 to customLabel4 on up to 100 products, models or categories, so ad campaigns can be split by your own groups ("season sale", "clearance"). This writes to the CRM only: the labels reach Google with the next hourly product push, and only if the owner armed that push — it never sends anything itself, never arms anything, and never touches the preview stamp. A product takes its own label, else its model's, else its category's (nearest ancestor). customLabel0 is derived from each product's markup and is refused. Omit a slot to leave it alone; null or empty clears it. Returns { set, cleared, targets }; an id not in the workspace refuses the whole call. Idempotent. Use preview_google_merchant_products to see the labels in the body, and push_google_merchant_catalog to send sooner. The result echoes the workspace.

customLabel0.description: Not settable: customLabel0 is derived from each product's markup and is refused if sent. Use customLabel1 to customLabel4.

customLabel1.description: Value for customLabel1, at most 100 characters. Omit to leave the slot alone; null or an empty string clears it.

customLabel2.description: Value for customLabel2, at most 100 characters. Omit to leave the slot alone; null or an empty string clears it.

customLabel3.description: Value for customLabel3, at most 100 characters. Omit to leave the slot alone; null or an empty string clears it.

customLabel4.description: Value for customLabel4, at most 100 characters. Omit to leave the slot alone; null or an empty string clears it.

labels.description: The slots to set or clear. At least one of customLabel1..4.
