kind.description: What the id is. A model or category label applies to every product under it that has no label of its own.

targets.description: The products, models or categories to label, at most 100.

tools.name: list_ad_accounts
tools.description: List the connected ad channels with their accounts: per channel the provider key, label, health (active, setup_required, error), the last sync time, any current sync error, campaign counts, and each account's id, name, currency, status and last sync. Also returns reportingCurrency, the workspace currency every revenue and ROAS figure is stated in. Read-only, from stored state: no ad platform is called, so a figure is as fresh as the last hourly sync. Takes no arguments. Use list_ad_campaigns with a provider for campaigns, spend and results, and list_ad_recommendations for what the CRM suggests.

tools.name: list_ad_campaigns
tools.description: List one ad channel's campaigns for the last N days, biggest spend first: status, objective, daily or lifetime budget, currency, spend and clicks (from the ad platform), and what the CRM recorded for the campaign — leads, deals, won deals, orders, sales, revenue, costPerLead. roas is revenue divided by spend, and is null — never guessed — when the ad account's currency differs from reportingCurrency, because that would invent an exchange rate; revenue is in reportingCurrency only. Read-only, from stored state, no ad platform is called. Use list_ad_accounts for the provider keys, list_ad_recommendations for what to do next, and get_report for the CRM's own sales reports.

days.description: How many days back spend, clicks and results are summed, ending today. Default 30, at most 30 (the CRM keeps 30 days).

provider.description: The ad channel, as listed by list_ad_accounts (for example google or openai).

tools.name: list_ad_recommendations
tools.description: List the CRM's open advertising recommendations across every channel: kind (spend_no_result, unanswered_leads, low_roas, scale_winner, cost_per_lead_spike), severity (urgent, warning, opportunity), the campaign and the frozen evidence the rule saw. They are deterministic rules over data only the CRM has — whether a click became a customer, what it paid, whether anyone replied — not a model's opinion. Snoozed and handled ones are not listed. Read-only; deciding a recommendation is done on the Ads page. Takes no arguments. Use list_ad_campaigns for the figures behind a card and list_conversations for the unanswered enquiries.

tools.name: preview_google_shopping_campaign
tools.description: Dry run of a Google Shopping campaign, step 1 of 2: the very request create_google_shopping_campaign would send, validated by Google with validateOnly — nothing is created in the ad account. Returns { currency, payload } or Google's own refusal (a duplicate name above all). It does record that a dry run happened, which is the evidence the owner needs before arming campaign creation on the Ads page; it arms nothing and needs no owner switch. Needs a signed-in connection with the ads:write scope and a role that works with ads; an API token is refused because it carries no role. Show the person the payload before creating. Idempotent. Use list_ad_accounts for the account and currency, and create_google_shopping_campaign for step 2.

dailyBudget.description: Daily budget as a positive decimal string in the ad account's currency, for example '15.00'. Send only an amount the person stated. Refused if it is above the owner's cap.

labelIndex.description: Optional: which custom label slot (0 to 4) limits the campaign to a group of products. Needs labelValue.

labelValue.description: Optional: the value of that custom label, for example 'margin_high'. Needs labelIndex.

maxCpc.description: Maximum cost per click as a positive decimal string in the ad account's currency, for example '0.40'.

name.description: Campaign name, at most 128 characters. Google refuses a name already in use.

tools.name: create_google_shopping_campaign
tools.description: Create a Google Shopping campaign in the connected Google Ads account — step 2 of 2, after preview_google_shopping_campaign. A REAL write to the live ad account, but the campaign is always created PAUSED: this tool never activates or starts one, and spends nothing until a person starts it in Google Ads. It obeys the owner's own settings on the Ads page: refused unless campaign creation is armed there and the daily budget is within the owner's cap. It is also refused until the workspace owner switches on 'AI may create paused ad campaigns' (Settings → Integrations → Connect AI), and an API token is refused because it has no role — only a signed-in owner or administrator can create. Returns { campaignResourceName, status: 'PAUSED' }. Not idempotent: Google refuses a duplicate name. Never tell the user a campaign is running. Use list_ad_campaigns afterwards, once the sync has read it. The result echoes the workspace.

dailyBudget.description: Daily budget as a positive decimal string in the ad account's currency, for example '15.00'. Send only an amount the person stated. Refused if it is above the owner's cap.

labelIndex.description: Optional: which custom label slot (0 to 4) limits the campaign to a group of products. Needs labelValue.

labelValue.description: Optional: the value of that custom label, for example 'margin_high'. Needs labelIndex.

maxCpc.description: Maximum cost per click as a positive decimal string in the ad account's currency, for example '0.40'.

name.description: Campaign name, at most 128 characters. Google refuses a name already in use.

tools.name: get_listing_automation
tools.description: Read the listing automation of a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted), where a sale ends the listing: whether it lists the next unit after a sale and again when stock arrives, when (relistTiming: instant, next_run within 10 minutes, after_1h, after_6h, after_24h), its publishing windows in the workspace time zone, the daily limit, the refresh of listings that do not sell, the settings version, whether a dry run was done (previewAt), whether the connection's own publishing and removing are turned on (arming — only the owner turns those on, on the connection page), and the queue summary (open jobs by state, listed today, failed this week). Read-only. Use update_listing_automation to change it, preview_listing_automation for the dry run, list_listing_jobs for the queue itself.

platform.description: The marketplace whose listing automation this is. Only vinted has one today.

tools.name: list_listing_jobs
tools.description: List the listing automation's queue on a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted): listings waiting to go up (after a sale, after a restock, on schedule, or a refresh), with the product, when each is due and its state (pending, waiting_stock, waiting_delete, running) — or, with scope history, what was done, skipped, cancelled or failed and why. Paginated with a real total. Read-only. Use cancel_listing_jobs to cancel waiting ones and get_listing_automation for the settings.

platform.description: The marketplace whose queue to read. Only vinted has listing automation today.

scope.description: open: listings still waiting (soonest first). history: what the automation did or skipped, newest first, with the reason.

tools.name: preview_listing_automation
tools.description: Dry run of the listing automation on a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted), from the CRM's own data — nothing is sent to the marketplace. Counts live listings whose product has another unit (they would be listed again after a sale), listings of the last unit (they would wait for stock), listings of products whose stock the CRM does not count (never listed again), and sold or removed products still in stock (list them yourself), with sample names. Running it records that a dry run was done, which update_listing_automation needs before it may turn a behaviour on; show the person these numbers first. The result echoes the workspace.

platform.description: The marketplace whose listing automation this is. Only vinted has one today.

tools.name: update_listing_automation
tools.description: Change the listing automation of a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted). Send only the fields to change; the rest stay as saved. Changing when it lists (relistTiming, windows, maxPerDay) and turning a behaviour off work with the settings scope alone; turning relistAfterSale, relistOnRestock or the refresh ON also needs a dry run first (preview_listing_automation) and the workspace owner's switch for AI listing automation in Settings → Integrations → Connect AI, which is off by default. Once on, the CRM creates (and, for a refresh, takes down) listings on the live marketplace account by itself, only for products whose stock it counts. It never turns on the connection's own publishing: when that is off, the result carries the warning publishing_not_armed and nothing is sent until the owner turns it on. Turning a behaviour off cancels its waiting listings. Pass expectedVersion from get_listing_automation to avoid overwriting a change made meanwhile. Returns the saved settings, what was turned on and off, cancelled and warnings. Echoes the workspace.

expectedVersion.description: The settings version get_listing_automation returned. When given, the change is refused if someone saved meanwhile, instead of overwriting their change.

maxPerDay.description: At most this many new listings a day, spread evenly over the day's publishing windows; null removes the limit. Omit to keep it.

platform.description: The marketplace whose listing automation this is. Only vinted has one today.

refreshAfterDays.description: Take down and list again a listing that has not sold for this many days (14, 30 or 60), so it shows near the top again; null turns it off. It loses the listing's likes and views. Omit to keep it.

relistAfterSale.description: After a sale, list the next unit of the same product as a new listing. Only products whose stock the CRM counts. Omit to keep it.

relistOnRestock.description: List a product again once stock arrives, after it sold out or was taken down for having none. Listings a person took down stay down. Omit to keep it.

relistTiming.description: When a sold listing goes up again: instant (seconds after the sale's order is in the CRM), next_run (the automation's next pass, within 10 minutes — the default), after_1h, after_6h or after_24h. Omit to keep it.

windows.description: Publishing windows in the workspace time zone: new listings go up only inside them, e.g. [{"weekday":5,"from":"18:00","to":"22:00"}] for Friday evening (weekday 1 = Monday, times on 10-minute steps, "to" may be "24:00"). An empty list means any time. Omit to keep them.

tools.name: schedule_listing_publishes
tools.description: Queue products to be listed on a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted) within the listing automation's publishing windows and daily limit, a few at a time, instead of all at once — the same as the channel page's "Publish on schedule". Each queued product later goes up as a new listing through the same publisher as the Publish button, so a product missing something is reported in list_listing_jobs, not sent. Requires the connection's publishing to be turned on by the owner, and the owner's switch for AI marketplace publishing in Settings → Integrations → Connect AI. A product already listed, already queued or not on the channel is counted, never listed twice. Returns { queued, alreadyListed, alreadyQueued, notOnChannel }. Not idempotent beyond that guard. Echoes the workspace.

platform.description: The marketplace to publish on. Only vinted has listing automation today.

productIds.description: Product ids (1 to 100) from search_products or list_channel_products. Each must be a member of the channel without a live listing; the rest come back counted, never listed twice.

tools.name: cancel_listing_jobs
tools.description: Cancel listings waiting in the listing automation's queue on a one-item-per-listing marketplace (Vinted), by job id from list_listing_jobs. Nothing is sent to the marketplace and no live listing changes; the products simply are not listed for that reason. A job a run is sending right now, or one already closed, is not cancelled and comes back in notCancelled. Idempotent. Returns { cancelled, notCancelled } and echoes the workspace.

jobIds.description: Ids of queued listings (1 to 100) from list_listing_jobs. Only waiting ones are cancelled; one a run is sending right now, or already closed, comes back in notCancelled.

platform.description: The marketplace the listings were queued for. Only vinted has listing automation today.
